articles.title: Breast cancer survivor runs NYC Marathon topless to proudly show her mastectomy scars
articles.summary: Lauren Spiezia, a 33-year-old mother from New Jersey, completed the New York City Marathon on November 1, 2026, with her chest uncovered to raise awareness about breast cancer and encourage survivors to embrace their bodies.
articles.body:
Lauren Spiezia, a 33-year-old mother from New Jersey, completed the New York City Marathon on November 1, 2026, with her chest uncovered to raise awareness about breast cancer and encourage survivors to embrace their bodies.

Spiezia was diagnosed with stage-two breast cancer at 31, after initially being told she was too young for the disease to be a serious concern. Her treatment included 16 rounds of chemotherapy, six rounds of immunotherapy, a double mastectomy, reconstructive surgery, and the removal of her fallopian tubes following the discovery of a cancer-related genetic mutation.

After initially struggling with insecurity about her mastectomy scars, she decided to run the marathon with them visible as a symbol of strength and survival.

She completed the 26.2-mile race in 4 hours, 54 minutes, and 4 seconds. Her team raised approximately $50,000 for cancer research.

Although her decision generated mixed reactions online, Spiezia emphasized that her goal was to help patients feel less alone and encourage women to take their health concerns seriously.

articles.title: Arizona man swallowed by massive sinkhole that suddenly opened in his own backyard
articles.summary: A man in Phoenix, Arizona, was rescued after a large sinkhole opened in the backyard of his home on November 1, 2026.
articles.body:
A man in Phoenix, Arizona, was rescued after a large sinkhole opened in the backyard of his home on November 1, 2026.

Firefighters responded around 3 p.m. to a property near 24th Street and Thomas Road, where the man had fallen into a hole approximately six feet deep. He suffered a chest injury and was unable to climb out on his own.

A pickup truck had also partially fallen into the sinkhole, creating an additional hazard. Rescue crews stabilized the vehicle to prevent it from falling farther before sending a technician down to help the trapped man.

The rescue was successful, and the man was transported to a nearby hospital in stable condition. No firefighters were injured.

The exact cause of the collapse has not been confirmed, although a Phoenix Fire Department spokesperson suggested that heavy rainfall earlier that day may have contributed to the ground giving way.

articles.title: Stock Market Crash: Expert preaches calmness as buy or sell advice divides public opinion
articles.standfirst: Stock traders are wondering whether this is the right time to buy, or if the slide will continue.
articles.summary: Stock traders are wondering whether this is the right time to buy, or if the slide will continue.
articles.body:
The United States stock market is currently in shambles. Thursday, November 5 proved to be a negative turning point, as the Nasdaq, S&P 500, and Dow Jones all plummeted . The massive sell-off comes right after a strong Wednesday outing for the market.

What seems to be driving the crash is an extremely negative reaction to the midterm elections, which concluded on Tuesday night. There are fears among traders that a Democrat-led House and Senate could impose too many restrictions on tech companies ; particularly when it comes to AI development and data centers .

Despite the immense panic, many have pondered if this is actually a legitimate opportunity to buy low on stocks that were performing extremely well up until Wednesday. Some stocks began bouncing back throughout Thursday, but they are still very far from their normal stock prices. On the other hand, the fears about tech regulation isn't going away anytime soon .

Stock market crash presents a very intriguing buy-low opportunity

With that said, one of the leading commentary pages on social media focused on global capital markets has preached caution when it comes to reacting to Thursday's crash. The Kobeissi Letter believes some of the fears should be kept in check , specially because even Democrats can't "outright ban" the advancement of AI, as it doesn't behoove the country .

Given the calmness The Kobeissi Letter is preaching, it presents a real opportunity for traders who have been waiting for stock prices to go down. Some of these major stocks might never get this low again , unless something drastic happens in the future. This looks like the time to get in, with the caveat that there is still a lot of risk involved due to the changing political landscape.

articles.title: Was he qualified? Lead physician in Christa Pike's botched execution hadn't placed IV line since 2013
articles.standfirst: New details about Dr. Mark Fowler's medical experience have raised questions
articles.summary: New details about Dr. Mark Fowler's medical experience have raised questions
articles.body:
Tennessee officials had been warned about the medical qualifications of a physician involved in the state's lethal injection procedures months before Christa Pike survived an execution attempt that prompted the suspension of further executions.

Dr. Mark Fowler , appointed by the Tennessee Department of Correction, had not inserted a central intravenous catheter since 2013, according to testimony he provided under oath in 2025.

Despite that admission, Fowler was involved in the failed execution of Tony Carruthers in May 2026 and was subsequently selected to oversee Pike's lethal injection four months later.

Court documents seen by People reveal that Fowler also acknowledged having no hospital privileges to perform central line procedures, raising questions about the state's decision to retain him.

Those concerns became particularly significant after Pike 's September 30 execution attempt failed, leaving her hospitalized following complications with the administration of the lethal injection drug pentobarbital.

The revelations have intensified scrutiny of Tennessee's execution protocol and whether officials adequately responded to warnings about the experience of medical personnel involved.

Fowler 's role came under scrutiny following the May 21 attempted execution of Carruthers , when a three-person intravenous team struggled to establish the required access for administering lethal drugs.

According to a court declaration from Carruthers ' attorney, Maria DeLiberato of the American Civil Liberties Union, Fowler was called into the execution chamber after the initial attempts proved unsuccessful.

The physician then attempted to insert a central catheter in two locations, but neither procedure succeeded, and officials eventually abandoned the execution after more than an hour.

DeLiberato described Carruthers as being "clearly in pain" and "gutturally groaning," recalling that he repeatedly complained, "It hurts, it hurts."

The medical concerns extended beyond Fowler 's unsuccessful attempts, with anesthesiology expert Dr. Gail Van Norman questioning whether his experience met contemporary clinical expectations.

In a declaration reviewed by People, Van Norman concluded that Fowler lacked the recent training and practical experience generally necessary to maintain central line privileges at major hospitals.

She also characterized the technique described in the court evidence as a "violation of the current standard of care."

Botched execution prompts demands for accountability

The concerns surrounding Fowler resurfaced after Pike survived two doses of pentobarbital during Tennessee's September execution attempt.

Fowler subsequently attributed the failure to an improperly positioned intravenous line, which allowed the drug to enter surrounding tissue rather than circulate properly through her bloodstream.

Following the incident, Governor Bill Lee ordered an independent investigation and suspended the state's remaining scheduled execution for 2026.

Fowler has previously defended his experience, telling ProPublica that inserting a central line was comparable to riding a bicycle and disputing allegations that his hands shook during Carruthers ' procedure.

However, attorneys representing death row prisoners argue that the earlier failed execution should have prompted a thorough review before Tennessee proceeded with Pike 's case.

"These problems will keep happening until Tennessee takes meaningful steps to increase transparency, oversight, and accountability in the execution process," said Kit Thomas , deputy chief of the Federal Public Defender's Capital Habeas Unit in Middle Tennessee.

The controversy now extends beyond one doctor's qualifications, raising broader questions about medical oversight, execution procedures and the state's responsibility to address known risks.

articles.title: A NASA telescope falls to Earth: it was launched in 2004 and studied the most powerful explosions in the universe
articles.standfirst: In August, an attempt to extend its useful life had failed
articles.summary: In August, an attempt to extend its useful life had failed
articles.body:
After more than 20 years, a NASA telescope has fallen to Earth , as confirmed by the United States Space Force. Its function had been to detect and study gamma-ray bursts , considered the most powerful in the universe. As initially expected, most of the craft disintegrated upon entering our planet's atmosphere.

The statement released explains that it was the Swift telescope, weighing nearly 1,500 kilograms , and that it was moving in an orbit below 375 kilometers. The experts' question regarding the device was what was going to happen to the rest of it, specifically where it was going to impact. For that, the moment of reentry was crucial.

Finally, the remains have fallen over northern Sumatra island after 22 years of collecting data and after managing to survive far beyond its expected lifespan and after sending data from more than 2,000 explosions .

A complex operation could not divert the telescope in August

To extend its operating time, last August NASA set in motion a risky plan: it launched a motorized robot whose aim was to move the device away from Earth. However, this maneuver failed and forced the agency to follow a new course and analyze its fall, which has accelerated due to a solar storm this past weekend.

The Swift telescope consisted of three instruments, the first standing out for its ability to orient itself, turn and move within a few seconds, and point at the explosion with high precision. Its work has served the study of many astronomers, who have tasked Swift with a large number of observations over the last 22 years that it has been active.

articles.title: What does 100% permanent and total VA disability benefits mean? Everything you get with this rate
articles.standfirst: A permanent and total rating can provide financial support for veterans and their families
articles.summary: A permanent and total rating can provide financial support for veterans and their families
articles.body:
Thousands of American veterans depend on disability compensation to manage the lasting effects of military service, but those awarded a 100% permanent and total rating may qualify for financial assistance and additional benefits that are not always widely understood.

The Department of Veterans Affairs uses the designation, commonly abbreviated to P&T, when a veteran's service-connected disabilities warrant total compensation and are considered unlikely to improve significantly during their lifetime.

Unlike temporary disability ratings, permanent and total status generally protects recipients from routine future medical examinations, reducing uncertainty about whether their compensation will continue.

However, it doesn't mean every veteran receives identical payments or automatically qualifies for all available federal and state programs.

That is particularly important for veterans supporting spouses or children, as several additional benefits can significantly reduce household expenses.

How much does 100% permanent and total VA disability pay in 2026?

Under the VA's 2026 compensation rates, a veteran with a 100% disability rating and no dependents receives $3,938.58 per month in tax-free benefits.

That increases to $4,158.17 for someone with a dependent spouse, while a veteran with a spouse and one qualifying child receives $4,318.99 monthly.

Additional compensation may be available for dependent children or parents, as well as veterans whose disabilities qualify them for special monthly compensation.

However, the 100% rating and permanent designation serve different purposes.

A total rating establishes the level of compensation, while permanent status indicates that the VA does not expect the underlying disability or disabilities to improve.

Veterans can also receive payments at the 100% rate through Total Disability based on Individual Unemployability, commonly known as TDIU.

Unlike a standard schedular 100% rating, TDIU generally involves restrictions on substantially gainful employment, making it important to understand which classification applies.

What extra benefits are available to veterans with 100% P&T rating?

Healthcare is among the most significant advantages, with qualifying veterans generally receiving VA medical treatment and prescription medications without copayments.

Comprehensive VA dental care may also be available, covering treatment that many veterans with lower disability ratings would not otherwise qualify to receive.

Eligible spouses and dependent children can benefit from CHAMPVA, a healthcare program that helps cover medical expenses when they meet the relevant requirements.

Families may also qualify for Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance under Chapter 35, which provides financial assistance for approved college courses, vocational training and other education programs.

Property tax relief represents another potential benefit, although exemptions vary by state and may depend on residency, homeownership and disability requirements.

Additional privileges can include military commissary and exchange access, certain federal student loan discharge opportunities, and reduced fees for vehicle registration or recreational licenses.

Importantly, permanent and total status doesn't make a VA disability rating absolutely irreversible, although routine reassessments are generally not scheduled.

Veterans should review their official benefit letters and check individual program requirements before assuming they qualify for additional assistance.

Understanding those distinctions can help veterans secure the support available to them while avoiding confusion about what a 100% permanent and total disability rating actually guarantees.

articles.title: A child dies from measles in Wisconsin, the first death in the state since 1990
articles.standfirst: The Wisconsin Department of Health Services (WDHS) has recorded 431 measles cases in 13 counties so far this year
articles.summary: The Wisconsin Department of Health Services (WDHS) has recorded 431 measles cases in 13 counties so far this year
articles.body:
Health authorities confirmed the death of a baby due to measles in Wisconsin , recording the first death linked to the disease in the state since 1990 . The incident comes amid a critical resurgence of the disease in the United States.

The Wisconsin Department of Health Services (WDHS) has recorded 431 measles cases in 13 counties so far this year . Authorities detailed that 428 of these infections correspond to unvaccinated people.

In addition, the country is facing one of its worst outbreaks in decades, totaling more than 4,800 cases in 47 states by the end of October . This same week, the state of New York also reported its first measles death in 30 years.

Skepticism toward vaccines has caused different outbreaks

Although measles was declared eliminated in the U.S. in 2000, growing vaccine skepticism has led to the return of local outbreaks. Because of this, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) is considering meeting to assess whether the country should lose that public health distinction.

Experts reiterate that two doses of the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine offer effectiveness close to 97% and are the main tool for preventing serious complications such as pneumonia or brain inflammation.

The recommended vaccination schedule for the measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine (MMR: Measles, Rubella, and Mumps) is mainly organized into two doses to ensure long-term immunity. Depending on the official schedule of the country or region, the timing varies slightly.

In the case of the United States, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) recommend a first dose between 12 and 15 months of age and a second dose between 4 and 6 years of age .

articles.title: What if O.J. Simpson didn't act alone? Defense investigator raises chilling new questions in the Goldman-Brown case
articles.standfirst: More than 30 years after Nicole Brown Simpson and Ron Goldman were killed, a new Peacock documentary examines previously unseen photographs, unidentified fingerprints and claims involving people close to O.J. Simpson
articles.summary: More than 30 years after Nicole Brown Simpson and Ron Goldman were killed, a new Peacock documentary examines previously unseen photographs, unidentified fingerprints and claims involving people close to O.J. Simpson
articles.body:
The murders of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ron Goldman remain among the most widely discussed criminal cases in American history.

Now, a new two-part documentary is bringing fresh attention to the possibility that O.J. Simpson may not have acted alone on the night of June 12, 1994.

Titled OJ's Accomplice, the series premiered on Peacock on November 1. Directed by Ari Mark and Sumit David , it revisits evidence from the original investigation and features interviews with people who were connected to the case, including former defense investigator Pat McKenna, lead detective Tom Lange, Kato Kaelin and Nicole 's sister, Tanya Brown .

One of the most striking arguments comes from McKenna , who questions whether the physical evidence is consistent with Simpson confronting and fighting both victims without assistance.

The documentary presents photographs of Simpson taken the day after the killings. According to McKenna , the images show little visible damage beyond a cut on one of his fingers.

“We took all these pictures of O.J.,” McKenna , 78, explains before the documentary shows photographs that “have never appeared in a documentary” before.

“Here’s O.J.’s hand. He’s got one little cut, but this is not a guy who’s just killed two people. He’s got no bruises. He hasn’t got a black eye. He’s got nothing, not even a bad lip, the guy has.”

He then questions whether Simpson could have overpowered Goldman without help.

“So, if it’s O.J. Simpson , maybe he went to kill Nicole . But then, fighting Ron Goldman, that’s going to take more than one person. It has to be two people.”

These are McKenna's interpretations of the photographs, rather than proof that another person was present. Nevertheless, they form part of the documentary's wider examination of evidence that its filmmakers believe deserves another look.

The mystery surrounding Charlie and Joey Ippolito

Another important element concerns nine unidentified fingerprints reportedly recovered in connection with the investigation.

The documentary says the prints have never been matched to an individual and that requests to have them checked again through fingerprint databases were declined by the Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office and the LAPD.

The series also revisits Simpson's 2007 book, If I Did It, in which he described a hypothetical version of the murders involving an accomplice named Charlie. In that account, the character was portrayed as someone who accompanied Simpson and could have helped dispose of evidence.

The documentary examines whether the fictional name might have been connected to a real person, Charlie Ehrlich , a friend of Simpson who was later involved in the former football star's 2007 Las Vegas armed robbery case.

Ehrlich has maintained that Simpson told him the name was simply a placeholder and that he was not the person described in the book.

However, the documentary takes the theory further by considering Joey Ippolito, a deceased former drug smuggler who had connections to Simpson's circle.

In a recorded conversation, Ehrlich claims that Ippolito's brother told him Joey had admitted involvement in the murders.

That allegation is not independently established. Ippolito's widow has also criticised the documentary, describing the project as misleading and disputing the claims made about her late husband.

The theory has received additional attention following separate reporting by The New York Times about allegations made by Ippolito's brother, Sam, concerning Joey's movements and a heavy bag on the night of the killings.

Those claims have not established that Ippolito participated in the murders, and they remain allegations rather than proven facts.

The documentary also revisits the role of A.C. Cowlings, Simpson's longtime friend who drove the white Ford Bronco during the infamous 1994 police chase.

Ultimately, the series does not provide a definitive answer about whether Simpson had an accomplice. Its central claims remain theories that would require further corroboration.

The legal history is also important: Simpson was acquitted of the murders in his 1995 criminal trial, but a civil jury found him liable for the deaths of Brown and Goldman in 1997. He died in April 2024, aged 76.

As one participant concludes: “I don’t think we’ll ever know if there were accomplices for this murder.”

OJ's Accomplice is available to stream on Peacock, with both episodes examining questions that have surrounded the case for more than three decades.

articles.title: Chaos in prison: Newly released audio exposes catastrophic failure in Christa Pike's botched execution
articles.standfirst: Emergency crews were left waiting outside a Tennessee prison as officials struggled to verify a desperate call for medical assistance after the death-row inmate survived a lethal injection attempt
articles.summary: Emergency crews were left waiting outside a Tennessee prison as officials struggled to verify a desperate call for medical assistance after the death-row inmate survived a lethal injection attempt
articles.body:
Newly released emergency recordings have exposed a deeply troubling breakdown in communication after Tennessee's attempt to execute Christa Pike went wrong, with firefighters and paramedics apparently unable to reach the prison while officials argued over whether the emergency was genuine and which agency had authority to escort them inside.

The incident unfolded on September 30, 2026, at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville.

Pike , 50, had been given two doses of pentobarbital as part of the state's lethal injection procedure but remained alive. She was unconscious and experiencing abnormal breathing, prompting an urgent request for an ambulance.

However, recordings of conversations between emergency dispatchers, police and correctional officials reveal that medical responders were left waiting outside the facility as the situation was being verified.

According to recordings obtained by RadarOnline.com, Nashville's Department of Emergency Communications received the first notification at approximately 8:40 p.m.

Firefighters and paramedics were subsequently dispatched, but security requirements prevented them from entering without police assistance or the necessary verification.

One dispatcher expressed frustration about the situation, saying: "We need to send police hot because someone is at the front gate that's telling them that this is real and they need to enter."

The recordings show uncertainty over whether Metropolitan Nashville Police or Tennessee Highway Patrol should provide an escort.

Metro Police reportedly declined to take responsibility because Riverbend is a state-operated correctional facility, leaving dispatchers attempting to establish which agency could get responders through the gates.

Another dispatcher stressed the urgency of the request, explaining: "There's someone at the gate telling them to come in because ... they need the ambulance and that this is real."

The confusion was particularly alarming because the people waiting outside were not responding to an unverified routine incident. The emergency involved a prisoner who had just undergone an execution procedure and was reportedly still breathing.

An attorney from Tennessee's Office of the Post-Conviction Defender, identifying herself as Kelly Gleason , also contacted emergency services to explain the seriousness of Pike's condition.

"She's still alive and breathing and needs immediate life-saving care," Gleason told the dispatcher.

She also reported that Pike was unconscious and had been observed snoring after receiving the execution drugs.

A half-hour of confusion as responders waited outside

Further recordings reviewed by WSMV and other news organisations provide a clearer picture of the delay.

Responders were reportedly staged outside Riverbend by approximately 8:56 p.m. At 9:03 p.m., however, a dispatcher relayed information that the emergency had been classified as a false call and that no medical assistance was required.

Four minutes later, a responder reported that someone at the prison gate was insisting the situation was real and demanding that emergency crews enter. The call was not officially validated until approximately 9:11 p.m., around 31 minutes after the initial notification.

At 9:08 p.m., Gleason's call was also logged. A dispatcher subsequently warned colleagues that the attorney was repeatedly seeking information, saying: "The defense attorney by the name of Kelly Gleason is calling us and asking on an update. So it's escalating,"

The recordings do not establish precisely how much the delay affected Pike's medical outcome. Nevertheless, they raise serious questions about why a request for emergency treatment following an execution attempt could be mistaken for a false alarm, and why agencies appeared unable to agree on a procedure for getting medical personnel inside.

Pike was eventually taken to hospital after surviving the two doses of pentobarbital. She spent time unconscious and on a ventilator, with her lawyers initially fearing she might not recover. She was discharged on October 10 and returned to the Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center.

In a statement reported by Reuters on October 30, Pike described continuing physical and emotional pain and said she remained isolated in a prison hospital ward. Her attorneys have also raised concerns about the constitutionality of the execution attempt.

Tennessee Governor Bill Lee ordered an independent review of what happened and suspended the state's remaining scheduled executions for 2026. The state's Department of Correction maintained after the incident that it had followed the established execution protocol.

The newly released audio adds another disturbing dimension to an already extraordinary case.

Beyond the failure of the lethal injection procedure itself, investigators now face questions about the emergency response, the prison's communication systems and the safeguards intended to ensure that someone in immediate medical danger can receive help.

articles.title: The untold story of Nancy Green, the woman who made Pearl Milling Company famous
articles.standfirst: Her story is one of American entrepreneurship, racial stereotypes, advertising history and a remarkable human being
articles.summary: Her story is one of American entrepreneurship, racial stereotypes, advertising history and a remarkable human being
articles.body:
Long before celebrities signed multimillion-dollar endorsement deals, social media influencers promoted products to millions of followers, or professional athletes became the faces of major advertising campaigns, a woman named Nancy Green helped establish the concept of the modern brand ambassador. Born into slavery in Kentucky in 1834, Green became the original face of Aunt Jemima pancake mix after captivating millions of visitors at the 1893 World’s Columbian Exposition in Chicago . Her ability to entertain crowds while preparing pancakes helped turn a relatively unknown food product into a national commercial success.

Yet, despite spending three decades representing one of America’s most recognizable food brands, Green died in 1923 and was buried in an unmarked grave at Chicago’s Oak Woods Cemetery. It took nearly a century for her resting place to receive a proper headstone.

Her story is one of American entrepreneurship, racial stereotypes, advertising history and a remarkable woman whose contributions were overshadowed by the fictional character she was hired to portray.

From slavery to the World’s Columbian Exposition

Nancy Green was born into slavery in 1834 in Kentucky. Following the Civil War and the abolition of slavery, she eventually moved to Chicago, where she worked as a cook and housekeeper for the prominent Walker family. Her life took an unexpected turn in 1890 when she was recommended for a commercial opportunity by a member of the Walker family.

The story of Aunt Jemima had begun a year earlier in Missouri. Newspaper editor Chris Rutt and mill owner Charles Underwood had purchased a flour mill in St. Joseph and were looking for a way to sell their surplus flour. Their solution was a ready-made pancake mix that consumers could prepare simply by adding water and cooking it in a skillet.

They needed a recognizable name and marketing identity. Rutt borrowed the name Aunt Jemima from a blackface minstrel performance he had encountered, drawing on a racist caricature of a Black domestic servant. The product was subsequently sold to businessman R.T. Davis, who saw an opportunity to transform the character into a powerful advertising attraction.

Davis discovered Green in Chicago, where she was already known for her cooking abilities. At 59 years old, she auditioned for the role and was hired to represent the product. Her major opportunity arrived in the spring of 1893, when Chicago hosted the World’s Columbian Exposition , one of the largest international exhibitions in American history.

The event attracted approximately 27 million visitors over six months, providing an extraordinary platform for businesses to showcase their products and innovations. Green became one of its most popular attractions.

The woman who turned pancake demonstrations into a marketing phenomenon

At the exposition, Green prepared pancakes at the company’s booth beside an enormous flour barrel, entertaining visitors with songs and stories while demonstrating the product. Some of the stories were based on her own experiences, while others were written to reinforce the fictional Aunt Jemima character created for the advertising campaign.

The crowds became so large that special police officers were reportedly needed to manage the lines of visitors waiting to see her. The commercial results were extraordinary. By the time the exposition ended, the company had reportedly received more than 50,000 orders. Green also received a medal and certificate recognizing her showmanship at the fair. Davis subsequently signed her to a lifetime contract and promoted her as the “Pancake Queen.”

Her success represented something relatively new in American advertising: a real person becoming the public face and living embodiment of a commercial product.

Today, celebrities, professional athletes and entertainers regularly receive substantial compensation to promote brands. Green’s story offers an early example of that business model, although the racial stereotypes underlying her particular role make it a complicated chapter in advertising history.

For approximately three decades, she traveled throughout the country, appearing at fairs, festivals and public exhibitions to promote Aunt Jemima pancake mix. In 1914, the R.T. Davis Milling Company even changed its name to the Aunt Jemima Mills Company, demonstrating how influential the character had become in the company’s commercial identity.

The real Nancy Green was much more than Aunt Jemima

One of the most overlooked aspects of Green’s life was her involvement in Chicago’s African American community.Away from advertising appearances and pancake demonstrations, she dedicated considerable time to religious and social causes . Green helped establish Olivet Baptist Church, which became one of Chicago’s most important Black religious institutions. The congregation eventually grew to more than 9,000 members at its peak.

She also worked as a missionary, organized antipoverty initiatives and advocated for equal rights. These activities paint a picture of a woman whose influence extended well beyond the commercial world. While the Aunt Jemima character was built around a fictionalized and stereotypical portrayal of Black domestic workers, Green was helping establish institutions and strengthen a community during a period when African Americans faced significant racial discrimination and economic barriers.

On August 30, 1923, Green died in Chicago after being struck by a vehicle involved in a collision with a truck. She was reportedly standing on a sidewalk when the accident occurred. Her death was covered by the Chicago Defender, one of the most influential African American newspapers of the era. However, the woman who had spent decades promoting a nationally recognized brand was buried in an unmarked grave at Oak Woods Cemetery.

Quaker Oats acquired the Aunt Jemima brand in 1925 , just two years after Green’s death. Over subsequent decades, several other women portrayed the character. Anna Robinson became the model for the familiar illustrated portrait on the packaging. Chicago blues singer Edith Wilson later portrayed Aunt Jemima in television advertising, while Aylene Lewis appeared as the character at Disneyland’s original Aunt Jemima restaurant when the theme park opened in 1955.

Eventually, PepsiCo acquired Quaker Oats in 2001, bringing Aunt Jemima under the umbrella of one of the world’s largest food and beverage companies. In June 2020, following the murder of George Floyd and the nationwide protests against racial injustice, PepsiCo announced that it would retire the Aunt Jemima name and image.

The company acknowledged that the branding was based on a racial stereotype and said the change was necessary to move away from imagery associated with America’s history of racial discrimination.

In 2021, the product was relaunched under the name Pearl Milling Company, returning to the original name of the Missouri mill where the pancake mix had been developed in 1889.

articles.title: Social Security 2027 Maximum Taxable Earnings: How much will your SS be taxed next year?
articles.standfirst: The Social Security Administration has raised the amount of income subject to payroll tax in 2027, meaning higher earners will contribute more next year
articles.summary: The Social Security Administration has raised the amount of income subject to payroll tax in 2027, meaning higher earners will contribute more next year
articles.body:
A merican workers will face a higher Social Security payroll tax threshold in 2027, following the Social Security Administration's (SSA) announcement that the maximum amount of annual earnings subject to the tax will increase to $192,300.

The new figure represents a $7,800 increase from the 2026 limit of $184,500. It means employees earning above the threshold will pay Social Security tax on a larger portion of their income, although the amount collected from each paycheck will depend on their salary and how frequently they are paid.

The adjustment is part of the annual process through which the government updates the Social Security taxable maximum in response to changes in average wages.

It is important to understand that the limit applies to earnings subject to Social Security contributions, not the amount of retirement benefits someone can receive.

For employees, the Social Security tax rate remains at 6.2% in 2027. Employers pay an additional 6.2% on the same wages, bringing the combined contribution to 12.4%.

Consequently, someone earning at least $192,300 will pay a maximum of $11,922.60 in Social Security taxes during 2027. That is $483.60 more than the maximum employee contribution of $11,439 in 2026.

Self-employed workers face a different calculation because they are responsible for both portions of the Social Security contribution. Their rate is 12.4%, meaning the maximum payment will reach $23,845.20 next year.

When will high earners stop paying Social Security tax in 2027?

The new threshold will have a particularly noticeable effect on people with substantial salaries because they can reach the taxable maximum much earlier in the year.

For example, someone earning $1 million annually would reach the $192,300 limit on March 12, 2027, assuming their salary is earned evenly throughout the calendar year. After crossing that threshold, they will no longer have Social Security tax deducted from their remaining wages for that year.

A worker earning $500,000 annually would reach the limit around May 21 under the same calculation, while someone earning $60,000 would continue contributing throughout the year because their total salary remains below the taxable maximum.

The distinction becomes even more striking when comparing the effective contribution rates. Someone earning $192,300 pays 6.2% of their salary towards Social Security . A person earning $1 million pays the same maximum dollar amount, meaning their effective Social Security tax rate is considerably lower.

However, the taxable maximum does not apply to Medicare in the same way. Medicare's standard 1.45% employee tax continues across all covered earnings, without an income ceiling. Workers earning more than $200,000 also face an additional 0.9% Medicare tax on income above that threshold.

The 2027 adjustment comes alongside a separate increase in Social Security benefits. The SSA has announced a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA), taking effect in January 2027.

The agency estimates that the average retired worker's monthly payment will rise from $2,095 to $2,170, an increase of approximately $75 per month.

That increase is intended to help beneficiaries manage rising living costs, although the amount individuals actually receive will depend on their personal benefit calculations.

There is also a wider financial challenge facing the programme. The 2026 Trustees Report projects that the Old-Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund could exhaust its reserves in 2032 if Congress does not make changes.

At that point, continuing income would cover only around 78% of scheduled benefits, according to the trustees' projections.

For workers, the immediate takeaway is straightforward: the 2027 taxable maximum is $192,300, and the highest employee Social Security contribution will be $11,922.60.

Those earning less than the threshold will continue paying 6.2% on their covered wages, while higher earners will stop contributing once their annual earnings reach the limit.

articles.title: Taurid Meteor Shower 2026: When is the peak of the 2026 Taurid meteor shower and what is the best place to see it in the USA?
articles.standfirst: The annual celestial display is famous for its unusually bright fireballs rather than huge numbers of shooting stars
articles.summary: The annual celestial display is famous for its unusually bright fireballs rather than huge numbers of shooting stars
articles.body:
November brings another opportunity for stargazers across the United States to witness one of the year's most distinctive meteor showers.

The 2026 Taurid meteor shower is particularly interesting because it features two separate streams, giving observers more than one opportunity to spot a shooting star streaking across the night sky.

The Southern Taurids reached their November peak around November 4–5, but the Northern Taurids are expected to reach their maximum around November 11–12. That means the main viewing opportunity still lies ahead for anyone who missed the earlier display.

According to NASA's November skywatching guide, both showers are relatively modest, producing approximately five meteors per hour under ideal conditions.

However, the Taurids have a reputation for producing exceptionally bright fireballs, which can make them particularly impressive despite their relatively low numbers.

The American Meteor Society also lists November 11–12 as the peak period for the Northern Taurids , with the shower remaining active until December 10. Consequently, anyone unable to watch on the exact peak night can still look for meteors on surrounding evenings.

When and where should you watch the Taurids?

The most important dates to remember are November 4–5 for the Southern Taurids and November 11–12 for the Northern Taurids . The latter is the next major opportunity for viewers in the United States.

There is another reason to be optimistic about the viewing conditions. The Northern Taurids reach their maximum shortly after the November 9 new moon, meaning relatively little moonlight should interfere with the display.

A darker sky makes it easier to distinguish fainter meteors, although cloud cover and artificial lighting can still affect visibility.

The best time to head outside is around midnight local time, when the constellation Taurus , from which the meteors appear to originate, climbs higher in the sky.

However, observers should avoid looking directly at the constellation's radiant. Instead, it is better to watch a broad area of sky some distance away, where meteor trails can appear longer and more noticeable.

What is the best place to see the Taurid meteor shower in the USA?

For Americans hoping to find particularly favorable conditions, Big Bend National Park in Texas is one of the strongest choices.

The National Park Service describes Big Bend as one of North America's outstanding stargazing destinations, noting that it has the least light pollution of any national park unit in the lower 48 states.

Its remote location, far from major urban areas, helps preserve exceptionally dark skies. The park also holds International Dark Sky Park status, making it an excellent destination for observing astronomical events.

Another excellent option is Big Bend Ranch State Park, also in Texas. The Texas Parks and Wildlife Department identifies it as having some of the darkest skies in the state, with certain areas reaching a Bortle Class 1 rating, the darkest category on the scale used to measure night-sky conditions.

Other possibilities include Death Valley National Park in California and Nevada, as well as Arches National Park in Utah.

Both feature protected dark-sky environments that offer excellent opportunities for astronomy enthusiasts. The National Park Service highlights more than 40 units in its system that have received International Dark Sky Place certification.

Watching the Taurids does not require an expensive telescope or specialist equipment. In fact, the naked eye is generally the best way to observe meteor showers because it allows viewers to take in a much wider section of the sky.

NASA recommends finding a dark location and allowing approximately 30 minutes for your eyes to adjust.

Avoid checking your phone frequently, since bright screens and flashlights can interfere with night vision. Bringing a reclining chair, warm clothing and a blanket can also make a long viewing session more comfortable.

It is also important to manage expectations. The Taurids are not comparable to the much more prolific Perseids or Geminids, and there may be long stretches without a visible meteor.

Their appeal comes from the possibility of catching a particularly brilliant fireball rather than counting dozens of shooting stars.

For those who miss the Northern Taurids, November still has another major astronomical event approaching: the Leonid meteor shower, expected to peak around November 17–18. December will then bring the Geminids, one of the most active annual meteor showers.

For now, however, the Northern Taurids offer the next opportunity to enjoy a spectacular November night under the stars.

articles.standfirst: The latest Powerball jackpot has reset to $20 million after a single ticket in New Jersey claimed Wednesday's enormous $847 million prize
articles.summary: The latest Powerball jackpot has reset to $20 million after a single ticket in New Jersey claimed Wednesday's enormous $847 million prize
articles.body:
Powerball players are preparing for another chance to become millionaires as the lottery returns with an estimated $20 million jackpot on Saturday, November 7, 2026.

However, anyone looking for the latest winning numbers will have to wait a little longer. The Saturday drawing has not yet taken place, meaning the five white-ball numbers, red Powerball and any jackpot-winning tickets remain unconfirmed.

The drawing is scheduled for 10:59 p.m. Eastern Time, with results expected to become available after the numbers are selected and officially verified.

Players should check the official Powerball website or their state lottery's results page rather than rely on unofficial number predictions.

The advertised jackpot stands at $20 million, with an estimated cash value of $8.6 million for a winner who chooses to receive a lump-sum payment instead of the annuity.

Saturday's prize represents a significant reset following Wednesday's historic result. A single ticket sold in New Jersey matched all six numbers on November 4, ending a lengthy jackpot run and securing one of the biggest prizes in Powerball history.

For now, the November 7 drawing offers players a fresh opportunity, although the odds of hitting the jackpot remain extremely challenging.

Previous Powerball results: New Jersey ticket claims $847 million prize

Before Saturday's drawing, the most recent Powerball numbers came from Wednesday, November 4.

The winning combination was:

- White balls: 15, 34, 41, 53, 56

One ticket sold at Wegmans Food Market on Farm View in Montvale, New Jersey, matched all six numbers to win the advertised $847 million jackpot.

According to the New Jersey Lottery, the winner can choose between receiving the full advertised prize through 30 increasing annual payments over 29 years or taking an estimated lump-sum payment of $363.1 million. Both amounts are before taxes.

The jackpot was the ninth-largest in Powerball history and the second-largest prize awarded during 2026. The retailer that sold the winning ticket is also set to receive a $30,000 bonus.

The result brought an end to a jackpot run that had attracted considerable attention across the country. It also meant Saturday's prize returned to the game's starting jackpot level of $20 million.

More than one million tickets won cash prizes in Wednesday's drawing, demonstrating that players can still receive smaller payouts without matching every number.

Saturday, November 7 winning numbers: Not yet available. The official results will be published following the 10:59 p.m. ET drawing.

How to play Powerball and what are the odds?

Powerball tickets cost $2 per play. Players select five white-ball numbers between 1 and 69, followed by one red Powerball number between 1 and 26. Alternatively, they can ask a retailer for a Quick Pick, allowing the lottery terminal to generate a random combination.

The jackpot is awarded to anyone who matches all five white balls and the red Powerball . The overall odds of winning the top prize are approximately 1 in 292.2 million, while the odds of winning any prize are around 1 in 24.9.

Players can also add the Power Play feature for an additional $1 per play. This option increases eligible non-jackpot prizes through a multiplier drawn separately. With Saturday's advertised jackpot below $150 million, the 10X multiplier is available, although it does not increase the jackpot itself.

Powerball drawings take place three times each week: Monday, Wednesday and Saturday. Ticket sales deadlines vary depending on the state or jurisdiction, so players should check local rules before purchasing.

The game is available across 45 states, Washington, D.C., Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. Ticket sales also expanded to the United Kingdom in July 2026.

Although the $20 million jackpot is considerably smaller than Wednesday's prize, it remains a potentially life-changing amount. Players should remember that every number combination has the same chance of being drawn, and previous results do not make particular numbers more likely to appear.

Once Saturday's drawing has taken place, the official Powerball website will publish the winning combination, Power Play multiplier and prize information. Until then, the November 4 numbers remain the latest confirmed results.

articles.title: Just a few hours to evacuate: How an unstable volcano in Spain could trigger megatsunami on the US East Coast
articles.standfirst: Researchers have debated whether a catastrophic Canary Islands landslide could generate destructive transatlantic waves
articles.summary: Researchers have debated whether a catastrophic Canary Islands landslide could generate destructive transatlantic waves
articles.body:
Millions of Americans living along the East Coast could face a devastating natural disaster if part of a volcano in Spain's Canary Islands collapsed into the Atlantic Ocean, according to a scientist who has spent decades studying the possibility.

Professor Bill McGuire , a British volcanologist, has renewed concerns about Cumbre Vieja on La Palma, where the western flank has long attracted attention because of its geological instability.

Unlike a conventional volcanic eruption, the scenario involves an enormous section of the mountainside breaking away and plunging into the sea, displacing enough water to generate a powerful tsunami.

McGuire believes such a collapse could produce waves reaching approximately 65 feet along parts of the United States coastline, with some simulations suggesting they could arrive within nine hours.

The warning has attracted considerable attention because of the limited time that might be available for emergency evacuations once a tsunami began crossing the Atlantic.

However, the scenario remains highly disputed, and there is no evidence that such a collapse is imminent or that coastal communities currently face an emergency.

McGuire 's concerns stem partly from fractures that developed along Cumbre Vieja 's western flank during an eruption in 1949, raising questions about the long-term stability of the volcanic ridge.

Research conducted during the 1990s suggested that parts of the mountainside were moving slowly toward the ocean, potentially creating conditions for a major landslide over geological timescales.

"Based on extensive studies, I expect this part of the flank will eventually crash into the North Atlantic, launching a megatsunami in the process," McGuire wrote in BBC Science Focus.

One early computer simulation suggested that an enormous collapse could create waves hundreds of meters high near La Palma before sending destructive energy across the Atlantic.

Under that extreme scenario, waves approximately 20 meters high could reach Florida within nine hours, potentially threatening densely populated coastal areas.

McGuire acknowledged the uncertainty surrounding the timing of such an event, suggesting that it could occur centuries or even millennia from now.

Why scientists disagree about danger to US East Coast

Despite the alarming projections, other researchers believe the potential consequences have been exaggerated by early models that assumed an enormous section of the volcano would collapse simultaneously.

More recent simulations have generally predicted substantially smaller waves reaching North America, with some estimates suggesting heights of approximately three to seven feet.

The US Geological Survey has also emphasized that a catastrophic collapse of Cumbre Vieja is unlikely in the foreseeable future.

Nevertheless, volcanic landslides can produce deadly tsunamis, as demonstrated when Indonesia's Anak Krakatau volcano partially collapsed in December 2018, killing more than 400 people.

McGuire argues that the destructive potential of these events makes continued monitoring essential, particularly on islands with active volcanoes and steep coastlines.

Modern technology allows scientists to track ground movements, seismic activity and changes in volcanic structures that could indicate developing instability.

Although a future collapse remains possible, no reliable prediction establishes when it might happen or how large the resulting waves would be.

The distinction is crucial: the nine-hour estimate describes a hypothetical tsunami's travel time, not an imminent evacuation deadline for Americans living along the East Coast.

articles.title: Blow to Trump’s Project: Judge Temporarily Blocks Controversial Washington Arch
articles.standfirst: Federal District Judge Tanya Chutkan has put the matter on hold
articles.summary: Federal District Judge Tanya Chutkan has put the matter on hold
articles.body:
Federal District Judge Tanya Chutkan has temporarily blocked for 14 days the start of construction on Donald Trump 's Arc de Triomphe in Washington, D.C. The injunction was issued just one hour after the National Capital Planning Commission (NCPC) approved the project by eight votes in favor and four against.

The judge prohibited any construction activity in the area after admitting the lawsuits filed by the administrations of Washington D.C. and the state of Virginia, as well as war veterans and conservation specialists. The arguments include the impact on local traffic, possible economic repercussions, and damage to the historical heritage .

The design envisions a structure about 76 meters tall inspired by the Arc de Triomphe in Paris

The design envisions a structure about 76 meters tall inspired by the Arc de Triomphe in Paris , topped by golden statues of an angel and eagles to commemorate the 250th anniversary of American independence. Likewise, the structure would be erected in Memorial Circle, next to the Arlington Memorial Bridge .

Veterans' associations and Democratic lawmakers denounce that its size breaks the visual and solemn connection between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery. A view shared by aviation experts and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), who are assessing the risks of erecting a structure of that height less than three kilometers from Ronald Reagan National Airport .

For his part, Trump has defended the project, arguing that it would also serve as a national security facility to house drones and sniper posts. The court will use these two weeks of suspension to examine the merits of the challenges to the legality of the project before the Administration can begin the work.

Its selection includes family-sized meals, salads, pasta dishes and ready-to-heat favorites, although prices and availability can differ between warehouses.

One of the more interesting recent additions is the Kirkland Signature Teriyaki Chicken with Sushi Rice bowl. Spotted in early November, the dish contains chicken thighs with teriyaki-style sauce and sushi rice.

It costs approximately $5.99 per pound, with containers weighing around two pounds and selling for under $12.

That makes it a relatively affordable option compared with restaurant takeout, although some shoppers question whether one container really provides two or three meals.

For smaller households, it could be a convenient dinner with leftovers, but bigger appetites may finish it in one sitting.

Another popular choice is Kirkland Signature Braised Beef with Yukon Mashed Potatoes. The hearty combination costs approximately $8.96 per pound and offers several servings, making it an appealing option for colder evenings.

Shoppers have praised the tenderness of the beef and the convenience of having the main course and side together.

For something that can be served cold, the Kirkland Signature Greek Pasta Salad with Rotisserie Chicken and Dressing is another option.

It returned to Costco during 2026 and costs around $4.99 per pound. The combination of pasta, chicken, feta, olives, vegetables and Greek dressing makes it suitable for lunches, gatherings or a quick meal.

From comfort food to a complete Thanksgiving dinner

Costco's mac and cheese is another relatively inexpensive prepared-food option. A recent price comparison estimated it at approximately $4.53 per pound, with a typical tray costing around $17. Shoppers can add bacon, extra cheese or crushed crackers to give it a little more flavor and texture.

The warehouse's rotisserie chicken also remains a versatile purchase. It can be served as a straightforward dinner or used in wraps, salads and tacos over the following days.

Costco shoppers have also recommended its stuffed peppers, chicken street taco kit and beef chili, although the availability of individual dishes varies.

For shoppers planning a larger celebration, Costco has a particularly substantial seasonal offer: an online-only Thanksgiving dinner package priced at $199.99, reduced by $70 from its regular $269.99 price. The promotion is advertised through November 30, while supplies last.

The approximately 30-pound package is designed to feed up to eight people. It includes a five-pound turkey breast, mashed potatoes, macaroni and cheese, sweet corn, green bean casserole, cornbread stuffing, candied yams, gravy, cranberry relish, dinner rolls, pumpkin pie and apple cobbler.

That works out to approximately $25 per person for a group of eight. However, it is not a completely ready-to-serve dinner: the turkey needs roasting and the sides require preparation or reheating.

The package is also online-only, so shoppers should not expect to find it in the refrigerated deli section.

Ultimately, the best value depends on how many people are eating and how much preparation shoppers want to avoid.

The teriyaki chicken bowl and pasta salad offer relatively inexpensive everyday options, while the Thanksgiving package provides a more complete solution for holiday hosting.

Costco regularly rotates its prepared-food selection, so shoppers should check their local warehouse or the retailer's website before making a special trip. Prices can change with location and package weight, and seasonal promotions are subject to availability.

articles.title: Benjamin Franklin, Founding Father of the United States: "An investment in knowledge always pays the best interest"
articles.standfirst: The famous saying captures the importance of education and personal development, but there is a surprising detail behind its connection to Benjamin Franklin
articles.summary: The famous saying captures the importance of education and personal development, but there is a surprising detail behind its connection to Benjamin Franklin
articles.body:
Few historical figures are as closely associated with practical wisdom as Benjamin Franklin .

The American Founding Father built a reputation as a scientist, inventor, writer and diplomat, while his observations about money, hard work and self-improvement continue to circulate centuries after his death.

One of the most popular sayings attributed to him is: "An investment in knowledge always pays the best interest".

It suggests that education should be viewed as something more valuable than an expense, because the skills and understanding gained through learning can create opportunities throughout a person's life.

The comparison with financial investment is particularly effective. Money placed in a savings account or investment can generate returns, but knowledge can provide benefits that extend far beyond a single financial reward.

It can improve decision-making, encourage independence and help people adapt when circumstances change.

However, there is an important historical qualification. Despite appearing on countless quotation websites and motivational posters under Franklin's name, the saying cannot be verified as his work.

Research into the quotation traces its earliest known appearance to the Daily Evening Transcript newspaper in Boston in November 1848.

A longer version appeared in the same publication in February 1849, almost six decades after Franklin died in 1790. The Library of Congress reference book Respectfully Quoted also identifies the attribution as unverified.

The saying may reflect Franklin's philosophy, but there is no documented evidence that he personally used those exact words.

Why Franklin believed education could transform lives

Franklin's own experiences help explain why the quotation became so closely associated with him.

Born in Boston in 1706, he received relatively little formal education before becoming an apprentice printer. He moved to Philadelphia as a teenager and gradually established himself as a successful businessman, publisher and intellectual.

Rather than relying on traditional schooling, Franklin continued learning throughout his life. In 1727, he established the Junto, a discussion group in Philadelphia where members exchanged ideas, debated subjects and explored ways to improve their community.

He also helped establish the Library Company of Philadelphia in 1731, one of America's earliest subscription libraries. The initiative reflected his belief that access to books and information should not be restricted to wealthy individuals.

His commitment to education extended into higher learning. In 1749, Franklin published proposals for improving education in Pennsylvania and helped organize the institution that eventually became the University of Pennsylvania.

His vision included practical subjects alongside traditional academic disciplines, preparing students for careers in business, government and public service.

Franklin's achievements were not limited to education. His scientific experiments helped advance understanding of electricity, while inventions such as the lightning rod, bifocals and Franklin stove demonstrated how knowledge could be applied to everyday problems.

His political career was equally influential. He became one of the key figures in the American Revolution, helped draft the Declaration of Independence and played an important diplomatic role in securing French support for the American cause.

The lasting value of investing in knowledge

The message behind the famous quotation remains relevant because education does not necessarily end when someone leaves school or university.

Learning new skills can help workers progress professionally, allow entrepreneurs to make better business decisions and give individuals greater confidence when dealing with unfamiliar situations.

It can also have benefits that are difficult to measure financially. Understanding history, science, technology and different cultures encourages people to question assumptions and approach problems from different perspectives.

Franklin's life provides a particularly strong example of this principle. His limited formal schooling did not prevent him from becoming one of the most influential Americans of the 18th century. Curiosity, experimentation and a willingness to keep learning helped shape his career.

Although the famous investment quotation should not be presented as a verified Franklin statement, its underlying message is consistent with many of his documented activities.

His efforts to establish libraries, support education and promote practical knowledge demonstrate how seriously he regarded intellectual development.

Ultimately, the greatest return from learning may not be measured in dollars. Knowledge can create opportunities, strengthen communities and remain useful long after material possessions have lost their value.

articles.title: Do VA benefits include vision? Eye exams, eyeglasses and everything that can be covered by your benefits
articles.standfirst: The Department of Veterans Affairs covers routine eye examinations and preventive vision testing for eligible veterans
articles.summary: The Department of Veterans Affairs covers routine eye examinations and preventive vision testing for eligible veterans
articles.body:
V eterans enrolled in VA health care can access a range of vision services, including routine eye examinations and tests designed to identify potential problems before they become serious.

However, coverage for eyeglasses and other vision aids is subject to additional eligibility requirements.

According to the Department of Veterans Affairs , veterans with VA health care benefits are entitled to routine eye exams and preventive testing, including screening for glaucoma.

These services are intended to help identify changes in vision and detect conditions that could affect long-term eye health.

To arrange an appointment, veterans can speak with their VA primary care provider or contact the eye clinic at their nearest VA medical center. The VA may also provide more specialized treatment when medically necessary.

Eyeglasses are not automatically provided to every veteran enrolled in VA health care. Instead, the department has specific eligibility categories that determine who can receive prescription glasses at VA expense.

Veterans may qualify if they have a compensable service-connected disability, are former prisoners of war, or have received a Purple Heart.

Other qualifying circumstances include receiving benefits under Title 38, United States Code, Section 1151, or an increased pension because they are permanently housebound or require regular aid and attendance.

There are also medical circumstances that can make someone eligible. These include vision problems caused by an illness being treated by the VA , such as diabetes, multiple sclerosis, vascular disease or a stroke.

Eye problems resulting from treatment, surgery, prescribed medication or a traumatic brain injury may also qualify.

What about contact lenses and specialist vision care?

The VA distinguishes between ordinary contact lenses and those required for medical reasons. Routine contact lenses are generally not covered, but medically necessary lenses may be provided for certain eye conditions.

Laser vision correction is another important distinction. Procedures such as LASIK and PRK are considered elective, and the VA does not perform them as part of its standard vision care provision.

Veterans experiencing significant sight loss may have access to additional support. The VA offers blind and low-vision rehabilitation services, which can help people maintain independence and manage everyday activities despite visual impairment.

These services can include assessments, rehabilitation training and specialist equipment designed to help veterans adapt to reduced vision. Eligibility depends on individual needs and the services recommended by VA specialists.

There are also rules about where prescriptions must originate. If a veteran receives an eye examination through a VA-authorized community care provider, the prescription for glasses must generally be filled through the VA .

Community care referrals for eye appointments do not automatically include the provision of eyeglasses.

Similarly, the VA will not fill prescriptions for glasses issued by an unaffiliated outside provider. Veterans should therefore check with their VA health care team before arranging an examination elsewhere.

How can veterans arrange vision care?

The first step is to contact a VA primary care provider or local medical center and ask about an optometry appointment. Veterans who need community-based treatment should discuss eligibility and obtain authorization through their VA health care team before booking with an outside provider.

Anyone who is unsure whether they qualify for prescription glasses can contact the prosthetic representative at their nearest VA facility. The VA can review the relevant medical and eligibility circumstances.

Ultimately, routine eye examinations and preventive testing are available through VA health care, but prescription eyewear, contact lenses and rehabilitation services have more specific requirements. Checking eligibility before ordering glasses or arranging outside treatment can help veterans avoid unexpected expenses.

articles.title: Will Rogers, Actor: "Good judgment comes from experience, and a lot of that comes from bad judgment"
articles.standfirst: The celebrated American entertainer became famous for his sharp observations about everyday life, although historical research suggests this particular saying may not have originated with him
articles.summary: The celebrated American entertainer became famous for his sharp observations about everyday life, although historical research suggests this particular saying may not have originated with him
articles.body:
W ill Rogers remains one of the most recognizable American humorists of the early 20th century, remembered for turning everyday experiences into memorable observations about human behavior.

The saying, "Good judgment comes from experience, and a lot of that comes from bad judgment," is frequently attributed to the actor and comedian, capturing the kind of practical wisdom that made his humor so popular.

Its message is straightforward: people rarely develop sound judgment without making mistakes along the way. Experience is often gained through decisions that do not work out, and learning from those moments can help prevent similar errors in the future.

The quote also offers a reminder that mistakes do not necessarily represent failure. They can become valuable lessons, provided someone is willing to recognize what went wrong and make a different choice next time.

However, there is an important qualification to the attribution. Although the expression is widely circulated under Rogers' name, research into its origins has not established that he actually said it.

Quote Investigator traced an earlier version to a newspaper report published in 1932, in which the saying was presented as an anonymous observation. Rogers was still alive at the time, but there is no documented evidence connecting him to its creation.

Will Rogers built a career on humor and everyday wisdom

Born William Penn Adair Rogers on November 4, 1879, near Oologah in what was then Indian Territory, the entertainer grew up on a ranch in a Cherokee family. His early life helped shape the cowboy image that would become central to his public identity.

Rogers initially developed his skills as a trick roper, traveling with Wild West shows and performing internationally. He eventually moved into vaudeville, where audiences became just as interested in his remarks between tricks as they were in his rope work.

His career expanded significantly after joining the Ziegfeld Follies in 1915. He became a Broadway attraction before moving into motion pictures, appearing in more than 70 films.

His ability to transition from silent pictures to talking movies helped him remain a major Hollywood star.

But acting was only one part of his influence. Rogers also became a successful newspaper columnist and radio personality.

His syndicated writing reached millions of Americans, while his broadcasts allowed audiences to hear the conversational delivery that had made him popular on stage.

According to the Smithsonian, his newspaper column appeared in more than 550 publications, and he wrote over 3,600 columns during his career. His humor frequently addressed politics, public figures and the contradictions of American society.

The saying about judgment fits the broader image of Rogers as a commentator who valued common sense and the lessons people gained through everyday life. Nevertheless, the Will Rogers Memorial Museum warns that some quotations are incorrectly attributed to him.

Quote Investigator's research found that the expression circulated anonymously before later versions became associated with Rogers and other public figures. It also appeared in Rita Mae Brown 's 2001 novel Alma Mater, where it was described as an old saying.

Rogers died on August 15, 1935, in an airplane crash in Alaska alongside aviator Wiley Post. He was 55.

His legacy as an entertainer and social commentator remains considerable. Even if the judgment quotation cannot reliably be credited to him, its enduring popularity reflects the appeal of the practical, experience-based wisdom associated with his public persona.

articles.title: Are you getting your Social Security Payment this Wednesday, November 11? This is the list for the next payment
articles.standfirst: Veterans Day changes the usual November payment calendar, meaning some retirees and disability beneficiaries will receive their money a day earlier than expected
articles.summary: Veterans Day changes the usual November payment calendar, meaning some retirees and disability beneficiaries will receive their money a day earlier than expected
articles.body:
Millions of Americans are preparing for their next Social Security payment, but the November calendar contains an important change that beneficiaries should be aware of.

Although Wednesday, November 11, would normally be the second-Wednesday payment date, the Social Security Administration (SSA) has moved the deposit forward because it coincides with Veterans Day.

As a result, eligible recipients will not have to wait until Wednesday to receive their money. Instead, the next group of retirement, survivor and Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) beneficiaries is scheduled to receive its November payment on Tuesday, November 10.

The adjustment affects people whose birthdays fall between the first and 10th of any month and who receive benefits under the standard Wednesday payment system.

It does not mean they are receiving an additional check or a larger benefit. The money is simply being delivered one day earlier because of the federal holiday.

The change is particularly important for households that rely on Social Security to cover recurring expenses such as rent, groceries, utilities and medical costs.

Knowing the correct deposit date can help beneficiaries avoid planning around a payment that will not arrive on the day they originally expected. The SSA's official 2026 calendar confirms the revised November schedule.

Social Security payment dates for November 2026

The SSA generally distributes retirement, survivor and disability benefits across three Wednesdays each month. The date assigned to an individual depends on the birth date of the person whose earnings record is used to claim the benefit.

For November, the schedule has been adjusted because Veterans Day falls on the second Wednesday. The remaining payment dates are:

- Tuesday, November 10: Beneficiaries born between the 1st and 10th.

- Wednesday, November 18: Beneficiaries born between the 11th and 20th.

- Wednesday, November 25: Beneficiaries born between the 21st and 31st.

People who began receiving Social Security before May 1997 generally follow a different schedule. Their November payment was scheduled for Tuesday, November 3, rather than one of the Wednesday dates.

The same third-of-the-month payment arrangement generally applies to people who receive both Social Security and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) , although their SSI payment follows its own calendar.

Why is the November 11 payment arriving early?

Veterans Day is a federal holiday observed annually on November 11 to recognize people who have served in the United States Armed Forces.

In 2026, it falls on a Wednesday, which would ordinarily be the scheduled payment date for beneficiaries born between the first and 10th.

Federal holidays can affect the SSA's payment timetable. When a scheduled payment date falls on a holiday or weekend, the agency generally moves the deposit to the preceding business day.

That is why the November payment is arriving on Tuesday, November 10. The adjustment affects the timing rather than the value of the benefit, so recipients should not expect an extra payment because of the change.

The agency's offices will also be closed on Veterans Day, meaning anyone who needs assistance should take the holiday into account when planning to contact Social Security.

What about Supplemental Security Income recipients?

SSI follows a separate payment timetable from standard Social Security retirement and disability benefits. Payments are normally issued on the first day of each month, but the date is moved forward when the first falls on a weekend or federal holiday.

November 1, 2026, fell on a Sunday. Consequently, SSI recipients received their November payment early, on Friday, October 30.

The next scheduled SSI deposit is December 1, which covers that month's benefit. Another calendar adjustment will occur at the end of December: the January 2027 SSI payment is scheduled for Thursday, December 31, because January 1 is a federal holiday.

What should you do if your payment does not arrive?

Beneficiaries who do not see their money on the expected date should first check their bank account and confirm that their payment information is correct. A delay does not necessarily mean that their eligibility has changed or that their benefits have been suspended.

The SSA advises recipients to allow three additional mailing days after the expected payment date before contacting the agency about a missing check. People can also review their benefit information through their personal my Social Security account.

For those receiving direct deposits, checking with their financial institution may help establish whether the payment has been received but not yet appeared in the account.

The most important date for the next group is therefore November 10, not November 11. Beneficiaries born between the 1st and 10th should plan around Tuesday's deposit, while the remaining Wednesday payment groups will receive their money on November 18 and November 25.
