articles.title: Maya Angelou, American poet and civil rights activist: "I can be changed by what happens to me, but I refuse to be reduced by it"
articles.standfirst: The inspirational message about overcoming adversity remains one of the most widely shared quotations associated with Angelou, whose writing explored identity, dignity and the strength to keep moving forward
articles.summary: The inspirational message about overcoming adversity remains one of the most widely shared quotations associated with Angelou, whose writing explored identity, dignity and the strength to keep moving forward
articles.body:
Few writers have expressed the importance of personal resilience as powerfully as Maya Angelou .

The American poet and civil rights activist is remembered for her reflections on overcoming hardship, and one of the sayings most frequently attributed to her captures that philosophy: "I can be changed by what happens to me, but I refuse to be reduced by it".

The message speaks to an experience familiar to many people: difficult events can leave a lasting mark, but they do not have to define an individual's entire life.

It recognizes that suffering, disappointment and injustice can influence someone's outlook without taking away their ability to decide who they want to become.

There is, however, an important detail about the wording. The version in the headline is widely circulated as an Angelou quotation, but Goodreads identifies it as a popular misquotation of a passage from her 2008 book Letter to My Daughter.

The wording in the book is: "You may not control all the events that happen to you, but you can decide not to be reduced by them."

Although the two versions are not identical, they communicate the same central idea. Angelou's original passage places the emphasis on the difference between what happens to a person and how that person responds.

It does not suggest that people can avoid pain or simply choose to forget difficult experiences. Instead, it encourages them not to allow those experiences to erase their sense of self.

How Maya Angelou's own experiences shaped her message

Understanding the quotation becomes particularly meaningful when considering Angelou's life. Born Marguerite Johnson in St. Louis, Missouri, on April 4, 1928, she experienced racism, instability and trauma during her childhood.

After suffering sexual abuse as a young girl, she became largely silent for several years. Literature, poetry and the support of people around her eventually helped her find a way to express herself again.

Her experiences became an important part of her literary voice. In 1969, she published I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings, the first volume of her autobiographical series.

The book described her childhood and adolescence, including the racism and abuse she endured. Its success established her as a major literary figure and helped bring the experiences of Black women into a wider public conversation.

Angelou's contribution extended beyond literature. During the civil rights movement, she worked with the Southern Christian Leadership Conference (SCLC), serving as its northern coordinator.

She also had connections with prominent activists including Martin Luther King Jr. and Malcolm X . Her work reflected a commitment to equality, dignity and the belief that individuals could help bring about meaningful change.

A legacy built around courage and self-worth

Angelou continued to write poetry, autobiographies and essays throughout her career. Her poem "Still I Rise" became one of her best-known works, with its defiant message of perseverance in the face of prejudice and attempts to undermine someone's dignity.

Another major public moment came in 1993, when she read "On the Pulse of Morning" at President Bill Clinton' s inauguration. She became the first African American woman to write and deliver a poem at a presidential inauguration, bringing her words to a national and international audience.

Her achievements were recognized with numerous honors, including the Presidential Medal of Freedom, awarded by President Barack Obama in 2010. Angelou died on May 28, 2014, at the age of 86, but her books and speeches continue to reach new generations.

The quotation associated with her name remains relevant because it offers a perspective that goes beyond simply telling people to be strong.

It acknowledges that life can change someone, sometimes profoundly, while insisting that adversity does not have to determine their value or limit their future.

That is the lasting power of Angelou's message: people cannot always choose what happens to them, but they can continue to shape the person they become.

articles.title: Veterans Day wreath-laying restrictions: Everything to know if you're attending the Memorial at Arlington National Cemetery
articles.standfirst: Visitors can still attend the national Veterans Day observance on November 11, but a major change means the public will no longer be able to watch the traditional wreath-laying ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
articles.summary: Visitors can still attend the national Veterans Day observance on November 11, but a major change means the public will no longer be able to watch the traditional wreath-laying ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
articles.body:
Americans planning to mark Veterans Day at Arlington National Cemetery in Virginia will need to pay attention to new restrictions affecting one of the day's most significant traditions.

The cemetery has confirmed that public access to the annual wreath-laying ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier will be restricted to official participants on Wednesday, November 11, 2026.

This represents a departure from previous years, when members of the public could gather to witness the solemn tribute.

However, the restriction does not mean Arlington is closing its doors to everyone wishing to attend the national commemoration.

The 73rd annual National Veterans Day Observance will remain free and open to the public, with the main program scheduled to take place inside the Memorial Amphitheater at 11 a.m.

The announcement is particularly important for visitors who may have assumed that attending the public event would also give them access to the wreath-laying itself.

Those are now two separate parts of the program, and only authorized participants will be permitted to attend the ceremony at the Tomb.

The cemetery has not publicly provided a detailed explanation for the change, so visitors should avoid assuming that the restriction applies to every activity taking place on the grounds.

What visitors can expect at the Memorial Amphitheater

Although the public cannot watch the wreath-laying ceremony, there is still a substantial program planned for Veterans Day.

The United States Coast Guard Band and the U.S. Air Force Singing Sergeants are scheduled to perform a musical prelude beginning at 10:30 a.m. The national observance will follow at 11 a.m., featuring a parade of colors by veterans' organizations and remarks from dignitaries.

Seating inside the Memorial Amphitheater will be available on a first-come, first-served basis. There is no admission charge, but visitors should arrive early because capacity is limited.

The cemetery has also introduced specific transportation arrangements for the event. Free parking will be available at the Welcome Center parking lot between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m.

However, visitors attending the observance must use the tram to travel between the Welcome Center and the Memorial Amphitheater.

Walking to and from the amphitheater is strictly prohibited during the event. Tram operations are expected to begin at approximately 8:30 a.m. and continue until capacity is reached. Arlington recommends arriving at the tram no later than 9:45 a.m. to improve the chances of securing access.

Security screening will also be mandatory before entering the cemetery and amphitheater.

Which items are prohibited?

Visitors should be particularly careful about what they bring. Arlington has published a list of restricted items, and security personnel may confiscate prohibited belongings.

Items that cannot be brought into the event include:

- Large bags and backpacks.

- Glass, metal or insulated containers, including hard water bottles and soda cans.

- Alcohol, coolers and picnic baskets.

- Tripods and selfie sticks.

- Weapons, ammunition, explosives and pepper spray.

- Aerosol containers, lighters and laser pointers.

- Air horns and other items considered potential safety hazards.

Clear disposable plastic water bottles are permitted. However, hard water bottles will be confiscated at the security checkpoint and will not be returned.

The cemetery also warns that the restrictions may be updated depending on security requirements. Visitors should therefore check the official announcement before setting off.

Can families still visit gravesites?

Yes. Family pass holders who need to visit the graves of loved ones can still enter through the main entrance on Memorial Avenue.

Nevertheless, they should expect delays when entering and leaving the cemetery. Movement restrictions and temporary freezes inside the grounds may affect visitors during the national observance.

Anyone unable to attend in person can also watch the event through the livestream announced by Arlington National Cemetery.

Why the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier matters

The restrictions are particularly notable because the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier has been central to national remembrance for more than a century.

The monument was dedicated on November 11, 1921, when an unidentified American service member from World War I was laid to rest following a national ceremony attended by President Warren G. Harding and international dignitaries.

It represents American service members whose remains were never identified, ensuring that those who died without their identities being known are still remembered and honored.

The opportunity for the public to lay wreaths at the Tomb has long been an important part of Arlington's commemorative traditions.

For anyone planning to attend this year's Veterans Day observance, the key distinction is simple: the Memorial Amphitheater program remains open to the public, but the wreath-laying ceremony itself is reserved for official participants.

Arriving early, following the transportation arrangements and checking the prohibited-items list will help visitors avoid unnecessary problems on November 11.

articles.title: William James, Philosopher and psychologist: "The great use of life is to spend it for something that will outlast it"
articles.standfirst: The influential American thinker believed that a meaningful existence should be measured by more than personal success
articles.summary: The influential American thinker believed that a meaningful existence should be measured by more than personal success
articles.body:
What makes a life worthwhile? For American philosopher and psychologist William James , the answer was not simply the pursuit of wealth, recognition or individual happiness.

Instead, he emphasized the importance of contributing to something with a value that extends beyond one's own existence.

His famous reflection, "The great use of life is to spend it for something that will outlast it," captures an idea that remains relevant more than a century after his death. It encourages people to consider the consequences of their actions and the kind of legacy they hope to leave behind.

The quotation is commonly associated with James , and research into its origins has traced an earlier version to a letter he wrote to Polish philosopher Wincenty Lutoslawski on November 13, 1900.

In that letter, the wording was recorded as: "The great use of a life," James said, "is to spend it for something that outlasts it." The letter was subsequently documented in the second volume of The Thought and Character of William James , edited by Ralph Barton Perry and published in 1935.

The central message is straightforward: a person's contribution can continue to matter long after their lifetime has ended.

That contribution does not necessarily have to involve a major historical achievement. Supporting others, sharing knowledge, creating something meaningful or working toward a better society can all represent ways of building a lasting legacy.

A thinker who helped shape modern psychology and philosophy

Born in New York City on January 11, 1842, James became one of the most influential intellectual figures in American history. Although he initially studied medicine at Harvard, his interests developed into psychology and philosophy, fields in which he would leave a substantial mark.

His 1890 publication, The Principles of Psychology, became a landmark work. It explored subjects including consciousness, memory, emotion, habit and the relationship between the mind and the body.

James also helped establish psychology as an academic discipline at Harvard, where he taught and influenced generations of students.

He was also a leading figure in American pragmatism, a philosophical approach that considers the practical consequences of ideas.

Rather than treating philosophy as an exercise detached from everyday life, James examined how beliefs and theories relate to human experience.

That outlook helps explain the enduring appeal of his words about spending life on something that will survive its creator. His philosophy placed considerable importance on the relationship between ideas, choices and their effects on the world.

James explored these questions in other influential publications, including The Varieties of Religious Experience (1902) and Pragmatism (1907). His work attracted attention from thinkers across different disciplines and continues to be studied today.

James died on August 26, 1910, aged 68, but his intellectual influence continued through his books, students and the development of modern psychology and philosophy.

Ultimately, his quotation offers a challenge to think beyond immediate rewards. It suggests that a meaningful life is not defined exclusively by what someone accumulates or accomplishes for themselves, but also by what they leave behind for others.

Whether through family, education, creativity, public service or personal relationships, the opportunity to make a lasting difference is available in many forms.

articles.standfirst: The Powerball jackpot has climbed to an estimated $30 million after the previous drawing produced no grand-prize winner
articles.summary: The Powerball jackpot has climbed to an estimated $30 million after the previous drawing produced no grand-prize winner
articles.body:
The latest Powerball drawing is scheduled for Monday night, meaning players will have to wait until after the draw to discover whether anyone has matched all six numbers and claimed the estimated $30 million jackpot.

According to the official Powerball website, the November 9 prize has an estimated annuity value of $30 million, while the cash option stands at approximately $12.9 million before taxes.

The drawing is scheduled for 10:59 p.m. Eastern Time, with winning numbers published after the results have been verified.

The previous drawing took place on Saturday, November 7, when the winning combination was 3, 36, 37, 56 and 61, with 21 as the red Powerball . The Power Play multiplier was 2X.

No ticket matched all six numbers, allowing the jackpot to continue growing for Monday's draw.

Players should check their tickets against the official results once the November 9 numbers become available rather than relying on unofficial predictions or numbers circulating before the drawing.

A new jackpot cycle follows the $847 million New Jersey win

The current prize comes after an extraordinary run that ended with a single ticket winning an $847 million Powerball jackpot in New Jersey.

The winning ticket for the November 4 drawing was purchased at Wegmans Food Market on Farm View in Montvale, Bergen County. Its numbers were 15, 34, 41, 53 and 56, with 21 as the Powerball and a 2X Power Play multiplier.

The prize was the ninth-largest jackpot in Powerball history. The winner can choose between receiving the advertised $847 million through an annuity or taking a one-time cash payment of $363.1 million, with both figures calculated before taxes. The winner had not been publicly identified in the latest reports.

Wegmans is also set to receive a $30,000 retailer bonus for selling the winning ticket. However, the company announced that the money would be donated to the Community FoodBank of New Jersey through its Check Out Hunger campaign, turning the sale into a contribution to local hunger-relief efforts.

How much could Monday's Powerball winner receive?

If a player wins the November 9 jackpot, they will face the familiar choice between an annuity and a lump-sum payment.

The advertised $30 million prize represents the annuity option, distributed through 30 graduated payments over 29 years. Alternatively, the winner can select the estimated $12.9 million cash value, which is paid as a single amount before applicable taxes.

Powerball tickets cost $2 per play, with players selecting five white-ball numbers from 1 to 69 and one red Powerball number from 1 to 26. The odds of matching all six numbers and winning the jackpot are approximately 1 in 292.2 million.

The optional Power Play feature costs an additional $1 and can multiply eligible non-jackpot prizes. It does not increase the advertised jackpot itself.

Monday's drawing is one of three regular weekly Powerball draws, which take place every Monday, Wednesday and Saturday. Ticket sales close at different times depending on the state or jurisdiction, so players should check their local lottery's deadline.

The November 9 winning numbers and Power Play result will be added once the drawing has taken place and the official results are confirmed. Until then, the $30 million jackpot remains up for grabs.

articles.title: Is Costco open on Veterans Day? This is the wholesale store schedule for Wednesday
articles.standfirst: The retailer follows a different holiday schedule from banks and government offices
articles.summary: The retailer follows a different holiday schedule from banks and government offices
articles.body:
Veterans Day brings changes to everyday schedules across the United States, with banks, government offices and several public services closing to recognize those who have served in the military. However, shoppers planning to visit Costco on Wednesday, November 11, should face little disruption.

The wholesale retailer is expected to operate its regular weekday schedule, meaning members can still purchase groceries, household essentials and other products despite the federal holiday.

Costco doesn't include Veterans Day among its nationwide warehouse closure dates, unlike Thanksgiving and Christmas, when locations across the country shut their doors.

However, customers should be aware that opening times are not identical for every membership category, with Executive Members receiving earlier access at participating locations.

Individual warehouses may also operate slightly different schedules, making it important to check local hours before heading out.

What are Costco opening hours on Veterans Day 2026?

Most Costco warehouses are expected to follow their usual Wednesday schedule, with Executive Members able to enter from 9 a.m. and shop until 8:30 p.m.

Gold Star and Business Members generally gain access one hour later, with their shopping hours running from 10 a.m. until 8:30 p.m.

The earlier opening for Executive Members is part of Costco's membership benefits, rather than a special arrangement introduced for Veterans Day .

However, these times aren't guaranteed at every warehouse. Costco advises customers to confirm their local store's schedule through its website or mobile application.

Shoppers planning to use additional services should also check operating times separately, particularly for pharmacies, gas stations, optical departments and tire centers.

These facilities can follow different schedules from the main warehouse, even when the store itself remains open.

Veterans Day is observed annually on November 11 to honor Americans who have served in the Armed Forces. Although federal offices typically close, private businesses are free to determine their own operating schedules.

Which holidays does Costco close its stores in 2026?

Costco follows a relatively extensive holiday closure policy compared with many other major American retailers, shutting its US warehouses on seven designated occasions each year.

The company's official schedule includes New Year's Day, Easter Sunday, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day.

With Veterans Day approaching, the next nationwide closure will be Thanksgiving on Thursday, November 26, 2026.

Warehouses are expected to reopen the following day, Friday, November 27, although customers should verify their local hours before visiting during the busy holiday shopping period.

Costco will subsequently close on Christmas Day, Friday, December 25, before observing New Year's Day on January 1, 2027.

Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve aren't included among its nationwide closure dates, although some locations may operate reduced hours.

This is important for members planning their shopping around the holiday season, particularly as several major celebrations fall within weeks of one another.

Wednesday's Veterans Day observance therefore shouldn't prevent Costco customers from completing their regular shopping, provided they follow their local warehouse's membership access times.

articles.title: What is Anthropic and why does its valuation exceed one trillion dollars?
articles.standfirst: The company behind Claude is preparing a historic IPO and will seek to raise more than $61 billion with its Nasdaq debut.
articles.summary: The company behind Claude is preparing a historic IPO and will seek to raise more than $61 billion with its Nasdaq debut.
articles.body:
Anthropic, the technology company behind Claude , is preparing one of the largest IPOs in history. The U.S. company submitted a new proposal to offer 825 million shares at a price of between $70 and $78 each, a deal that could place its valuation at around $1.33 trillion , according to estimates reported by The Wall Street Journal.

The deal could allow it to raise more than $61 billion on the stock market. The company is also considering a private placement of up to an additional $26 billion with major investors. Its debut is planned on the Nasdaq, under the symbol ANT, and the figure represents a considerable jump from the $965 billion it reached in its last funding round, in May 2026.

What Anthropic is and what it does with Claude

Anthropic is an artificial intelligence research and development company founded in 2021 by Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei, among other former researchers in the sector. Its best-known product is Claude , an artificial intelligence assistant capable of answering questions, analyzing documents, drafting texts, generating code, and helping solve professional tasks.

However, its business goes far beyond a chatbot. The company offers models and tools that other businesses can incorporate into their own systems, in addition to products such as Claude Code , aimed at software development, and solutions to automate workflows. Its customers pay for the use of the models or through subscriptions, allowing it to generate revenue from both the general public and the enterprise market.

Why is Anthropic worth so much money?

One of the main reasons for its valuation is the growth of its revenue. According to the information submitted by the company to U.S. regulators, Anthropic reported $17 billion in revenue during the third quarter of 2026. The figure represents a year-over-year growth of 1,127% , an expansion that helps explain investors' interest.

The company said its annualized revenue run rate reached approximately $81 billion at the end of October. This metric projects annual performance based on recent activity and does not equal the revenue it has already earned over a full fiscal year.

Another factor is the demand for its tools from large companies. Anthropic wants Claude to become part of companies' usual programming, analysis, and management processes, rather than being limited to providing answers to individual queries. That integration can translate into larger contracts and continued use of its services.

An IPO that also puts the AI sector to the test

The expected valuation comes at a time of heavy investment in artificial intelligence and growing concern over the cost of developing these systems.

Training and running advanced models requires data centers, specialized processors, and enormous amounts of energy. Anthropic needs to expand that infrastructure to meet rising demand, which entails very large financial commitments.

The deal also reflects a shift in market expectations. The company had previously been associated with a possible valuation of up to two trillion dollars , but the new offering benchmark falls below that figure. The volatility of tech stocks and doubts about the return on AI investments have led investors to examine costs and growth prospects more closely.

Millions of Americans have another opportunity to become multimillionaires on Tuesday, November 10, as the Mega Millions jackpot reaches an estimated $529 million following a succession of drawings without a grand prize winner.

The latest confirmed results remain those from Friday, November 6, when players competed for a $505 million jackpot that ultimately went unclaimed.

Drawing date: Friday, November 6, 2026

articles.title: Historic 1,000-foot ship, bigger than the Titanic, is about to be sunk to the bottom of the sea
articles.standfirst: A legendary ocean liner is preparing for one final voyage, but this time, it won't return to the surface
articles.summary: A legendary ocean liner is preparing for one final voyage, but this time, it won't return to the surface
articles.body:
T he historic SS United States is scheduled to be deliberately sunk off the coast of Florida on November 12, marking the end of an era for one of America's most recognizable passenger ships . Measuring more than 984 feet long, the vessel is even larger than the Titanic and is expected to become the world's largest artificial reef.

The operation will take place approximately 25 miles southwest of Destin, in the Gulf of Mexico. According to information reported by Infobae, citing EFE and CBS News, the ship will be towed from Alabama to the designated location, where crews will open its hatches to allow water to enter and gradually take the massive structure beneath the surface.

The ship will have a new purpose beneath the ocean

The project is being led by Okaloosa County, which purchased the SS United States in 2024 from the SS United States Conservancy. After efforts to find a financially viable way to preserve and restore the vessel failed, local authorities decided to give it a different future through an artificial reef project.

Before the sinking, specialized teams worked to prepare the ship for its new role. More than 100 fuel tanks were cleaned, and the decks were cleared as part of the environmental preparation. Once underwater, the structure is expected to provide surfaces and shelter for marine organisms, helping create a new habitat for different species. Local officials also see an economic opportunity in the project. The ship could become a major destination for divers, bringing visitors to the area and generating business for diving operators, hotels and other tourism services. However, the plan faces a potential obstacle after environmental conservation groups filed a lawsuit raising concerns about the possible consequences of sinking the vessel.

The SS United States leaves behind a piece of maritime history

Built in the early 1950s, the SS United States became a symbol of American naval engineering and was known for its speed during the golden age of transatlantic passenger travel . It connected the United States with European ports and was designed with the additional possibility of being converted into a troop transport ship if a military emergency required it.

The rise of commercial aviation eventually changed international travel, making large passenger liners less relevant. The SS United States stopped operating commercially toward the end of the 1960s . After spending decades out of service, it was towed from Philadelphia to Alabama in March 2025 as preparations for its eventual sinking continued. For the SS United States Conservancy, finding an alternative to dismantling the historic vessel was an important part of preserving its legacy . If the operation goes ahead as scheduled, the ship will begin a completely different chapter beneath the waters off Florida, trading its place in maritime history for a new role in the region's marine ecosystem.

articles.title: Minivan crashes into people outside Los Angeles metro station, killing 3
articles.standfirst: “We don’t know if it was done intentionally, if it was done by accident", Police said
articles.summary: “We don’t know if it was done intentionally, if it was done by accident", Police said
articles.body:
A minivan crashed into people outside a metro station in Los Angeles during rush hour Tuesday, killing three and critically injuring the driver and at least two others, authorities said.

The vehicle ended up under a food vendor’s tent after crashing at a busy intersection just before 6 p.m. in the North Hollywood neighborhood.

The driver, who is in his 60s, was taken out of the vehicle and was able to talk but appeared in shock, Los Angeles Police Capt. Warner Castillo said, adding that officials were not immediately able to determine the cause.

“We don’t know if it was done intentionally, if it was done by accident,” Castillo said at a news conference.

Investigators will go through video of the crash frame by frame, LAPD Chief Jim McDonnell said.

“It will be probably a prolonged but a very deliberate investigation to determine what happened here,” he said.

The minivan was on the sidewalk surrounded by debris Tuesday night with its driver's side door left open and an air bag deployed. Fire engines and emergency crews worked nearby as a helicopter flew overhead.

Luis Luna-Guzman was working at a burger stand nearby when he heard a loud boom and saw people on the ground along with food and cups. People nearby started running toward the crash.

As he moved closer, he found an injured woman lying near the bike racks, her face, arms and legs bloody, he said, recalling her eyes were closed as she moaned in pain.

“I told her, ‘Don’t move, help is coming,’” Luna-Guzman said, adding that he saw a woman's body nearby, while another woman was lying unmoving on the stairs leading to the station.

Mayor Karen Bass said the victims included street vendors and pedestrians.

“I’m heartbroken for the families of everyone impacted,” Bass said in a post on X.

Adrin Nazarian, a Los Angeles City Council member whose district includes North Hollywood, described the area as a close-knit community where there is always commotion and activity.

“This is a constantly very active place, so it’s extremely concerning when you hear something like this happen,” he said.

One entrance to the metro remained closed Tuesday night, but otherwise the property wasn't impacted and the stations for the bus and subway were open, according to Jose Ubaldo, spokesperson for the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority.

articles.title: What are the Chapter 30 VA additional benefits and add ons, and how can you apply to get them?
articles.standfirst: The Montgomery GI Bill offers more than monthly education payments, with eligible veterans potentially able to unlock thousands of dollars in additional benefits
articles.summary: The Montgomery GI Bill offers more than monthly education payments, with eligible veterans potentially able to unlock thousands of dollars in additional benefits
articles.body:
The Chapter 30 Montgomery GI Bill (MGIB-AD) can help veterans cover the cost of higher education and professional training, but the standard monthly payment is not necessarily the full extent of the support available. Depending on your military service, enlistment agreements and education history, you could qualify for several additional benefits that increase your payments, extend your education entitlement or help cover expenses associated with studying.

One of the most valuable options is the $600 Buy-Up program . Eligible service members can make additional contributions while serving, potentially increasing their monthly GI Bill payments by as much as $150. Over the full entitlement period, that can mean up to $5400 in additional benefits. However, there is an important restriction: you generally cannot purchase the Buy-Up after leaving the military. The additional contributions must have been made while you were serving, whilst another potential source of extra money is the College Fund , also known as the GI Bill Kicker . This provides additional monthly payments to veterans whose enlistment or reenlistment contracts included a qualifying incentive. The amount depends on the agreement, so checking your original military paperwork and education records is an important first step. For the October 2026 to September 2027 payment year, the full-time monthly Chapter 30 rate is $2601 for veterans with at least three years of qualifying active-duty service. Those with between two and three years qualify for a full-time rate of $2110. These figures exclude any applicable Buy-Up or College Fund additions. Applications can be submitted through the official VA education benefits website using VA Form 22-1990 . You should have your DD-214 , enlistment and reenlistment contracts, and evidence of any additional GI Bill contributions available. Your educational institution must also certify your enrolment before payments can begin. Veterans can contact the VA Education Benefits Department at 888-442-4551 , Monday through Friday, between 08:00 ET/05:00 PT and 19:00 ET/16:00 PT.

Rudisill decision and other Chapter 30 benefits you could claim

Veterans with multiple periods of active-duty service should pay particular attention to the Supreme Court 's Rudisill decision as it changed how the VA calculates education entitlement for certain veterans eligible for both Chapter 30 and Chapter 33 . Depending on their service history, eligible veterans could receive up to 48 months of combined education benefits rather than the usual 36-month limit. This is particularly relevant to those who reenlisted and completed separate qualifying periods of service. Chapter 30 also provides VA Tutorial Assistance , reimbursing eligible students for academic tutoring up to a lifetime maximum of $1200. Payments are generally capped at $100 per month, and students must demonstrate that tutoring is necessary. Applications use VA Form 22-1990t . The VA Work-Study Program allows eligible veterans to earn additional income while attending approved colleges or training program. Participants can work at VA facilities, educational institutions and veterans ' organizations, earning at least the applicable federal or state minimum wage. Apply using VA Form 22-8691 . Veterans pursuing professional qualifications may also receive reimbursement for licensing and certification examinations, potentially up to $2000 per exam. This includes qualifications in IT , healthcare , project management and construction . Applications require V A Form 22-0803 , proof of payment and examination details. Approved flight training can receive reimbursement of 60% of qualifying charges, while apprenticeships and on-the-job training may qualify for monthly education payments. The three areas particularly worth investigating are the Rudisill decision, the College Fund kicker and the $600 Buy-Up program . Each could make a meaningful difference to the education support available, but eligibility depends on your individual circumstances.

articles.title: Draft of Martin Luther King Jr.’s ‘I Have a Dream’ speech goes up for auction for millions
articles.standfirst: It was found by his widow in 1990, who kept it in her husband's desk until it came to light in 2024
articles.summary: It was found by his widow in 1990, who kept it in her husband's desk until it came to light in 2024
articles.body:
One of the great moments in history is Martin Luther King's speech... It is the final handwritten draft of the “I Have a Dream” speech , whose seven pages from a yellow notepad written in blue ink have gone up for auction. The starting price is 10 million dollars .

That speech was delivered before some 250,000 people at the March on Washington on August 28, 1963 and is one of the great memories of that moment. Hence its symbolism.

That is why Christie’s New York will offer them in a single-lot sale on January 22 , with an estimate of more than 10 million dollars , that is, about 8.6 million euros, and the proceeds will go to various charitable organizations.

As Christie’s manuscript specialist Peter Klarnet has explained, the pages include corrections and cross-outs that show the writing process. “Reading it, one feels as if they were there, beside Dr. King, watching him write it and edit it in real time” , he indicated.

The discovery of the manuscript and its public unveiling

His widow , activist and broadcasting executive Xernona Clayton , was the one who found the draft in the late 1990s in an envelope labeled ‘speech.’ That is why she decided to keep it in her husband’s desk until in 2024, with the support of Christie’s and her advisor Eddie Bridgeman, she brought it out again and they realized its historical significance.

The manuscript will be displayed for the first time at the National Center for Civil and Human Rights in Atlanta from November 16 to 22, and will then travel to Chicago and New York, where Christie’s will exhibit it at its 20 Rockefeller Plaza headquarters from January 15, King’s birthday, to January 21.

articles.standfirst: Nobody managed to claim the jackpot on Monday, November 9 meaning that it rolls over to Wednesday
articles.summary: Nobody managed to claim the jackpot on Monday, November 9 meaning that it rolls over to Wednesday
articles.body:
The Powerball jackpot has risen to $45 million for Wednesday, November 11 , after Monday's $31.5 million prize went unclaimed as the next winner could take home an estimated $19.4 million through the cash option, before taxes. Monday, November 9's winning numbers were 13, 34, 41, 45 and 48, with 25 drawn as the red Powerball and the Power Play multiplier was 2x, although nobody matched all six numbers or claimed the $1 million prize for matching all five white balls.

However, five tickets matched four white balls and the Powerball to win $50,000 each. A total of 273,677 winning tickets were sold, generating $1,783,166 in combined prizes meaning Wednesday's drawing carries an estimated $45 million jackpot and a $19.4 million cash option. The winning numbers will be available after the draw and the latest jackpot is considerably smaller than the $847 million prize won by a single ticket holder in New Jersey on November 4 as the winning ticket was purchased at a Wegmans in Montvale . Making it the second-largest Powerball prize awarded in 2026 and the ninth-largest in the game's history, the winning numbers were 15, 34, 41, 53 and 56, with 21 as the red Powerball and a 2x Power Play multiplier. New Jersey became the first and only state to produce a jackpot winner since August 15. The November 4 result was also the seventh Powerball jackpot won nationwide during 2026 and Montvale Mayor Mike Ghassali celebrated the news on social media, writing: "The second-largest prize ever was right here at Wegmans in the good ol' Borough of Montvale. What incredible news! Congratulations to the lucky winner."

How to play Powerball and what are the odds of winning?

The winner can choose between a one-time payment of $363.1 million or the advertised $847 million paid over 29 years. Both amounts are before taxes, and the ticket holder has until November 4, 2027, to claim the prize and has not come forward publicly. New Jersey allows Powerball winners to remain anonymous, although the winner must provide identification at lottery headquarters to claim the prize as state and federal taxes will be withheld. For those hoping for the same fate as the Montvale winner, the Powerball drawings take place every Monday, Wednesday and Saturday at 22:59 ET/19:59 PT and tickets cost $2, with players selecting five white numbers from 1 to 69 and one red Powerball from 1 to 26. The odds of winning the jackpot are approximately 1 in 292 million and the demand is high as the game is offered in 45 states as well as Washington, D.C. , Puerto Rico , the Virgin Islands and the United Kingdom . The biggest prize in Powerball history remains the $2.04 billion jackpot won by a ticket sold at Joe's Service Center in Altadena, California , in November 2022 as Edwin Castro was identified as the winner, choosing a lump-sum payment of $997.6 million rather than the advertised annuity.

articles.title: Rescuers search rubble for survivors after deadly Brooklyn building collapse
articles.summary: A three-story building collapsed Wednesday afternoon in Brooklyn’s Flatbush neighborhood, falling into an excavation beside a construction site. Firefighters and rescue crews rushed to the scene as images showed them climbing over the debris in search of people who might be trapped.
articles.body: A three-story building collapsed Wednesday afternoon in Brooklyn’s Flatbush neighborhood, falling into an excavation beside a construction site. Firefighters and rescue crews rushed to the scene as images showed them climbing over the debris in search of people who might be trapped. The collapse happened shortly after 4 p.m. on Flatbush Avenue. Crews searched through bricks and wood using hand tools, saws, search dogs and a drone. As night fell, lights from the rescue teams illuminated the wreckage and the scale of the damage. Authorities reported one person dead and at least 12 injured. Six of the injured were in critical condition, according to ABC7’s latest update. Rescue crews also pulled people alive from beneath the wreckage. The building fell toward the excavated lot next door. A neighboring building remained standing, but the collapse tore away part of its exterior wall, exposing rooms inside. City inspectors went to the scene to check the stability of nearby buildings. Rescue operations continued for hours as crews searched the debris and authorities urged people to avoid the area. Images of firefighters working atop the rubble captured the urgency of the search and the uncertainty facing people waiting for news of loved ones.

articles.body:
Last night, a three-story building collapsed in New York City , causing the deaths of at least two people and leaving 12 injured. Everything points to the possibility that more people could be trapped under the rubble, while rescue services assess the damage and work to pull out anyone who may still be at the scene of the incident.

A Fire Department official has explained to CNN that, apparently, at least one of the dozen injured remains trapped under the rubble. Likewise, it is believed that there could be more fatalities yet to be found , something that could be determined in the coming hours, once work on the ground progresses.

The cause of the collapse is unknown

Meanwhile, Lillian Bonsignore , Fire Commissioner, clarified that four of the injured are in critical condition , with no further details known at this time.

The incident occurred while several residents were inside and, after the collapse, rescue services quickly arrived in large numbers to remove the rubble, using excavators and heavy machinery.

articles.title: Can you just walk into a Social Security office without an appointment? These are the few cases when you can do it
articles.standfirst: Although the Social Security Administration encourages people to book appointments before visiting a local office, certain circumstances can qualify for same-day assistance, including urgent cases and people facing particular barriers
articles.summary: Although the Social Security Administration encourages people to book appointments before visiting a local office, certain circumstances can qualify for same-day assistance, including urgent cases and people facing particular barriers
articles.body:
Visiting a Social Security office without an appointment does not automatically mean you will be refused help.

While the Social Security Administration (SSA) has encouraged appointment-based services to manage demand and reduce waiting times, its guidance also recognizes that some people need assistance without being able to arrange a visit in advance.

The agency introduced a nationwide appointment-focused approach on January 6, 2025. The original announcement explained that appointments would be required for in-person services, including applications for Social Security cards.

However, it also made clear that people who could not arrange an appointment, or did not want one, would not simply be turned away.

The SSA specifically identified vulnerable individuals, military personnel, people with terminal illnesses and those requiring immediate or specialized attention as examples of people who could still walk into an office.

Importantly, the agency's subsequent internal instructions provided further detail about when staff should consider helping walk-in visitors on the same day.

Those instructions were made obsolete in April 2026, with the accompanying explanation saying the agency wanted to move away from an appointment-focused policy and allow offices to provide more same-day service.

That makes it important to distinguish between being allowed to request assistance without an appointment and having a guaranteed right to immediate service. Local office circumstances and the urgency of the case can still affect what happens when someone arrives.

Which situations can qualify for walk-in assistance?

The SSA's previous detailed guidance provides useful examples of circumstances in which same-day attention may be appropriate. These include:

People facing an urgent financial situation: Individuals experiencing dire need may require immediate help, particularly when a delay could have serious consequences.

People with terminal illnesses: The agency recognizes that individuals facing serious health circumstances may need more immediate or specialized attention.

Military personnel: Members of the military are specifically included among the groups that may receive walk-in assistance.

Vulnerable individuals facing barriers: People who struggle to access appointments or navigate the usual service channels may qualify for additional consideration.

Special Social Security number cases: Certain situations involving identity, employment verification, harassment, abuse or threats to personal safety can require more urgent handling.

Time-sensitive benefit cases: Issues involving immediate payments, critical pending claims or corrections to death records may also justify same-day attention.

The guidance additionally gives local office managers discretion to decide when an in-person visit should be handled immediately. Shorter transactions, known as Express Interviews, can also be completed at the first point of contact when appropriate.

Examples include benefit verification, submitting evidence, changing direct deposit details, requesting a 1099 form and updating an address.

However, these examples should not be interpreted as a guarantee that every visitor in one of these categories will automatically receive immediate service. The circumstances of the case and the office's ability to provide assistance matter.

How to arrange an appointment before visiting

For routine matters, booking ahead remains the safest approach. The SSA's online appointment service allows visitors to answer questions about the assistance they need and determine whether their issue can be handled online or requires a phone or in-person appointment.

People can also call the national Social Security number at 1-800-772-1213, Monday through Friday, from 8 a.m. to 7 p.m. in most U.S. time zones. Those who are deaf or hard of hearing can use the TTY number, 1-800-325-0778.

There are also reasons to consider completing business online instead. A personal my Social Security account allows users to access benefit information, check application progress, manage certain details and request replacement documents without travelling to an office.

The SSA's September 2026 performance figures showed that customers with appointments waited an average of approximately six minutes in field offices, compared with a longer average for visitors without appointments. Actual waiting times vary between locations.

Ultimately, walking into a Social Security office without an appointment can still be an option, particularly when a situation is urgent or requires specialized attention.

But anyone planning a routine visit should check the local office's arrangements and try to schedule ahead to avoid an unnecessary journey or lengthy wait.

articles.title: Black Friday 2026 Amazon: Best discounts, early deals, official dates and everything to know now about it
articles.standfirst: Amazon's biggest holiday shopping event is approaching, with millions of offers expected across technology, fashion, beauty and home products
articles.summary: Amazon's biggest holiday shopping event is approaching, with millions of offers expected across technology, fashion, beauty and home products
articles.body:
Amazon is preparing for one of its busiest shopping periods of the year, with its 2026 Black Friday and Cyber Monday promotions set to bring millions of discounts to customers across the United States.

Although Black Friday itself falls on November 27, shoppers will not have to wait until then to find offers.

Amazon has confirmed that its extended Black Friday Week and Cyber Monday event will begin on November 19 and continue through November 30, giving customers almost two weeks to look for bargains.

The retailer has also started promoting selected early offers, making November 12 a useful time to begin comparing prices and preparing shopping lists.

According to Amazon's announcement, this year's event will feature discounts across electronics, fashion, beauty, toys, kitchen equipment and household essentials. Major brands expected to participate include Samsung, Bose, Anker, LEGO, Hasbro, Le Creuset, HP, Google and Stanley .

What are the official Amazon Black Friday 2026 dates?

There are three important dates for shoppers to remember:

- November 19: Amazon's Black Friday Week begins at 12:01 a.m. Pacific Time.

- November 27: Black Friday, when additional limited-time promotions will be available.

- November 30: Cyber Monday and the final day of Amazon's announced event.

Amazon has also confirmed that some promotions will arrive before November 19, so customers can already browse its early offers rather than waiting for the main sale.

The biggest discounts Amazon has announced

The retailer has provided an early preview of several promotions, although individual prices and availability can change.

Among the advertised savings are:

- Fashion: Up to 50% off selected clothing from brands including Levi's.

- Beauty: Up to 40% off selected products from medicube and Color Wow.

- Toys: Up to 40% off selected LEGO and Hasbro Games products.

- Electronics: Up to 35% off selected products from Samsung, Bose and Anker.

- Kitchen appliances: More than $200 in savings on a Breville espresso machine.

- Home technology: More than $300 off a selected eufy robot vacuum.

- Fitness equipment: More than $300 off a selected NordicTrack treadmill.

Amazon devices will also feature prominently, with advertised reductions of up to 35% on selected products. Certain Kindle Colorsoft and Amazon Ember television models are included in promotions offering savings of up to 45%.

Another attraction will be Amazon's daily themed promotions, covering toys, technology, fashion, beauty, premium gifts and stocking fillers.

These offers will include limited-time discounts of up to 60%, with two separate deal drops on both Black Friday and Cyber Monday, scheduled for midnight and 8 a.m. Pacific Time.

Do you need Amazon Prime to access the deals?

No. Customers without a Prime subscription can shop the main Black Friday and Cyber Monday promotions. However, certain offers and benefits are reserved for members.

Amazon Prime costs $14.99 per month or $139 annually in the United States. Eligible new customers may also qualify for a 30-day free trial.

Shoppers can prepare by adding products to their wish lists, monitoring prices and setting deal alerts. Amazon has also promoted its Alexa for Shopping tools, which can track selected products and notify customers when prices fall.

The most important advice is not to assume every advertised percentage represents a genuine bargain. Compare prices across retailers, check historical pricing where possible and pay attention to product specifications before purchasing.

With the main event beginning November 19, shoppers still have time to prepare. The biggest discounts may arrive during the final weekend, but some early offers could be worth considering before popular products sell out. All advertised deals remain subject to availability and change.

articles.title: Jeff Bezos explains why so many people hate the rich: “You can be a billionaire even if you started a hamburger stand”
articles.standfirst: Amazon’s founder admits that young people have reasons to be angry
articles.summary: Amazon’s founder admits that young people have reasons to be angry
articles.body:
In recent years, the figure of the billionaire has gone from being a symbol of success to becoming, for many, the villain of the movie. Criticism of the concentration of wealth is growing, and rarely do we hear the version of those being talked about themselves.

Jeff Bezos has given his own. In an interview with Fox News journalist Bret Baier , recorded at Blue Origin’s headquarters in Florida, the founder of Amazon , the world’s second-richest person according to Forbes, with around $388.3 billion , answered why so many people see the rich as the enemy.

In his view, it is a matter of education: some people have been taught, "I believe incorrectly" , to see society as a struggle between oppressors and the oppressed and to regard success as something evil. “Success is not synonymous with evil,” he concluded.

To illustrate it, he turned to fast food: “You can be a billionaire even if you started a hamburger stand.” He gave as an example Raising Cane’s , the chicken chain founded by Todd Graves in Louisiana in 1996 , which today has nearly 1,000 locations in the United States .

Housing, the big problem Bezos does acknowledge

Despite his defense of the rich, Bezos admitted that the discontent is well-founded. “We have real affordability problems” , he acknowledged, referring to young people who cannot afford to live near their workplace because of housing costs. Even so, he rejected blaming landlords: according to him, the problem is one of supply and demand, and if demand is subsidized while construction is restricted, prices go up. He cited the case of Austin , which built around 120,000 homes between 2015 and 2024 and saw its rents fall.

The businessman ended with advice for the ballot box : be wary of the politician who points to culprits , because, in his view, they probably do not have solutions. His words did not convince everyone. A Pew Research survey found that one third of Americans aged 18 to 29 consider it immoral to be extremely rich, and former Democratic Senate candidate Amy McGrath reminded him on social media who now occupies the White House.

articles.title: A shooting in Washington leaves at least one dead and four injured near the White House
articles.standfirst: The incident occurred during the morning rush hour
articles.summary: The incident occurred during the morning rush hour
articles.body:
at least one dead and four injured this Thursday, November 12, in a shooting in the Logan Circle neighborhood of Washington, D.C. , approximately 1.6 kilometers (one mile) north of the White House . The incident was reported at around 8:20 local time during the morning rush hour , prompting a large deployment of security forces and the preventive lockdown of the area.

The shots were reported at the intersection of 15th Street NW and P Street, in the 1500 block of 15th Street. On that block are the VIDA Fitness gym, St. Luke's Episcopal Church, and various residential buildings . The Metropolitan Police Department (MPD) confirmed that at least five people were struck by the gunfire, but they have not yet specified the severity of the injuries or the medical condition of those wounded.

Multiple MPD emergency response teams quickly arrived at the scene

Police issued a shelter-in-place alert urging residents and passersby to remain inside buildings and away from windows. “I heard about four gunshots. They were spaced out, so I thought it was construction work, but then I saw police everywhere” , said Ryan Dubicki, a witness quoted by the newspaper El Mundo. Nearby schools were also closed.

In response to what happened, several MPD emergency response teams quickly arrived at multiple points in the neighborhood and cordoned off the surrounding streets. Officers from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) and members of the National Guard also moved into the area to assist with the operation.

Regarding the shooter , he has not been arrested . According to information circulated on social media, the suspect is believed to have barricaded himself inside a building in the 1500 block of 15th Street.

articles.title: SNAP enrollment plummets in nearly every state as millions of families face more changes
articles.standfirst: U.S. food assistance is experiencing a sharp decline following the changes approved in 2025. Nearly two million children would also have lost the benefit, while the government considers new restrictions.
articles.summary: U.S. food assistance is experiencing a sharp decline following the changes approved in 2025. Nearly two million children would also have lost the benefit, while the government considers new restrictions.
articles.body:
The SNAP food assistance program lost 5.5 million beneficiaries in the United States between July 2025 and July 2026, a 13% reduction that brought the number of participants down to 36.1 million, its lowest level in 17 years . The decline occurred after the approval of the budget law H.R. 1, which introduced changes to the eligibility and retention requirements for this aid.

The impact also reaches children. According to estimates by the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities (CBPP), around two million children may have stopped receiving assistance during that period. And the situation could become even more complicated: the Department of Agriculture introduced a new proposal to limit the conditions that allow certain families to automatically qualify for the program.

The new requirements behind the drop in SNAP

The reduction in beneficiaries is not solely due to an improvement in household incomes. The CBPP notes that the federal reform expanded work requirements for certain groups and shifted new administrative costs to the states.

Among the changes is the requirement to work or participate in training activities for at least 80 hours per month in order to keep the assistance, with exceptions предусмотрed for certain groups.

Difficulties completing the paperwork are also having consequences. People who could still meet the financial eligibility requirements may lose the benefit if they do not submit the required documentation on time.

Adding to this are the states’ new financial responsibilities, as they will have to assume a larger share of the program’s costs and face possible penalties related to their error rates.

The new proposal could affect another six million people

On November 10, 2026, the Department of Agriculture published a new regulatory proposal to restrict automatic SNAP eligibility. The initiative seeks to limit access for households that can currently receive food assistance because they are linked to certain state programs that help low-income families.

According to the Government's analysis cited by Associated Press, the change could leave approximately 6.3 million people without benefits by fiscal year 2029. The measure has not yet been approved and is open for public comment until December 10, 2026 . Therefore, these are not new benefit terminations that have already been carried out, but rather a possible additional cut.

The program’s evolution reflects the scope of the federal changes. Data compiled by the CBPP show that participation fell in every state except Alaska between July 2025 and July 2026.

With 36.1 million beneficiaries, SNAP is below the levels recorded before the pandemic, while the new proposal opens another front of uncertainty for the families who depend on this assistance.

articles.title: Who is the Washington, DC, shooting suspect? What we know so far
articles.standfirst: Police say the gunman opened fire at a VIDA Fitness gym and shot four other people before barricading himself in a nearby apartment
articles.summary: Police say the gunman opened fire at a VIDA Fitness gym and shot four other people before barricading himself in a nearby apartment
articles.body:
A shooting in Washington, D.C.’s Logan Circle neighborhood left one person dead and four others wounded Thursday morning, about a mile from the White House. Police said the suspected gunman later died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound after barricading himself in a nearby apartment building and speaking with negotiators for nearly an hour.

The violence began shortly before 8 a.m. at a VIDA Fitness gym near 15th and P streets Northwest. Police said one man was killed at the gym; four other people were shot and taken to hospitals. One was in critical condition, while the other three had injuries that were not considered life-threatening.

Witnesses described a sudden panic as people tried to leave. James Spellman, who was inside the gym, told the Associated Press that a man fell to the floor and another gym member rushed to help him. A fire alarm sounded as people began evacuating. Police arrived within about 30 seconds, according to interim Chief Jeffery Carroll.

Suspect barricaded himself in a seventh-floor apartment

As officers cleared a nearby residential building, gunfire came from the seventh floor, Carroll said. The suspect had barricaded himself inside an apartment.

Police negotiators spoke with him for about an hour before officers heard a gunshot and forced their way in. They found him with a self-inflicted wound; he was later pronounced dead at the scene.

The suspect has not been publicly identified. Police said they believe he lived in the apartment and was a member of the gym.

Carroll also said there appeared to have been a conflict between the suspect and the apartment building’s homeowners association, but authorities have not established that as the motive. Investigators are still working to determine what led to the shooting.

The standoff prompted a large police response, street closures and a shelter-in-place order for the surrounding area. Nearby schools were placed on alert.

Police later said the barricade had ended and lifted the shelter order, while asking the public to avoid the scene as the investigation continued. The FBI and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives assisted local authorities.

Mayor Muriel Bowser said the city was “devastated” by the loss of life. The White House was briefed, but officials said the shooting did not change its security posture.

articles.title: Anthropic sets IPO price that surprises some, and traders don't have much time before public date
articles.standfirst: The rising company known for its AI flagship product, Claude, will finally hit the stock market after a long wait.
articles.summary: The rising company known for its AI flagship product, Claude, will finally hit the stock market after a long wait.
articles.body:
As one of the leading companies in the AI race, it was only a matter of time before Anthropic went public in the stock market. The creators of Claude , one of the most used large language models (LLMs) in the world, Anthropic has seen a meteoric rise since being founded in 2021 by former members of Sam Altman 's OpenAI .

OpenAI hasn't gone public yet either . There have been rumors that it will happen in 2027, with shocking private estimates putting a potential share price for OpenAI between $734 and $910 . While OpenAI waits, Anthropic is beating them to the punch .

Anthropic to launch IPO on November 18 at up to $78 per share

In a filing to the SEC , Anthropic set in motion its IPO this week. If everything goes to plan, Anthropic stock will be available for public trading on November 19 . According to the company, 825 million shares will be offered at the time of its IPO . The price range per share is expected to be between $70 and $78 .

It’s a much more affordable entry point into the AI world within the stock market than OpenAI is expected to be. Of course, OpenAI has been around longer, but Anthropic had been operating at a much higher loss in net income through 2025 .

Going public should help Anthropic with their financials in a substantial way . Soon to be a six year old company and with major partnerships, the sky is the limit for Anthropic. And traders won’t have to splash too much cash to jump on board initially.

articles.title: Costco Edible Architecture Charcuterie Tree: How much it costs, where to find it, and what it’s made of
articles.standfirst: Costco is giving holiday entertaining a festive twist with a ready-to-assemble appetizer shaped like a Christmas tree
articles.summary: Costco is giving holiday entertaining a festive twist with a ready-to-assemble appetizer shaped like a Christmas tree
articles.body:
Forget traditional cheese boards for a moment: Costco has introduced a seasonal snack that could become a conversation starter at holiday gatherings.

The Edible Architecture Charcuterie Tree Kit turns familiar party-food ingredients into a decorative tree, giving shoppers a different way to serve appetizers without having to source every component separately.

The product has started appearing at selected Costco warehouses, attracting attention from shoppers looking for convenient ideas for Thanksgiving and Christmas entertaining.

Priced at $14.99, the kit weighs 17 ounces and provides the ingredients and equipment needed to assemble one large savory tree.

It is particularly appealing to hosts who want something that looks more elaborate than a standard platter but does not require hours of preparation. According to the manufacturer, putting the tree together takes approximately 15 minutes.

The finished centerpiece stands around 8.5 inches tall, making it suitable for a holiday table, appetizer station or buffet. Rather than arriving fully assembled, the kit gives customers the opportunity to build the display themselves using the included frame and instructions.

What comes inside Costco's charcuterie tree kit?

The Edible Architecture product is built around three main food components: sliced salami, fresh Asiago cheese and green olives.

These ingredients provide the savory foundation of the tree, with the meat and cheese arranged around a cone-shaped base to create its distinctive appearance.

The package also includes a sparkly star-shaped topper, toothpicks, the large tree cone and a step-by-step assembly guide. In other words, shoppers do not need to find their own structure or work out how to make the ingredients stay in place.

The manufacturer lists the Asiago cheese ingredients as cultured pasteurized milk, salt and enzymes.

Its Italian dry salami contains pork, salt and seasonings, while the green olives are pitted and combined with extra virgin olive oil. The kit contains milk, so anyone with a dairy allergy should take that into consideration before buying it.

Although the finished tree offers a mixture of meat, cheese and olives, its selection is relatively limited compared with a fully stocked charcuterie board. Hosts planning to feed a larger group may want to add crackers, grapes, nuts, additional cheeses or other cured meats.

That flexibility is part of the appeal: the tree can serve as the centerpiece, while extra snacks provide more variety for guests.

Where can shoppers find it, and is it available everywhere?

The product is being sold exclusively through Costco in selected regions. Edible Architecture lists availability in the Northwest, Southeast, all of California, including Northern California and San Diego, and Texas.

However, that does not mean every warehouse in those areas will have the kit. The product has appeared at a handful of locations, and availability can vary depending on local inventory and seasonal demand.

Shoppers should therefore check with their nearest warehouse before making a special trip.

The manufacturer's website also lists the Costco -exclusive version at $14.99, although its online listing has shown it as sold out. A separate, standard Edible Architecture Charcuterie Tree Kit is available through the company's website for $19.99, with cheddar and pepper jack replacing the Costco version's Asiago cheese.

The new Costco find has already attracted positive reactions online. One Instagram commenter praised the convenience, writing, "Love that it comes with everything," while another called it "the perfect party package!"

Ultimately, the $14.99 price makes the tree an accessible option for shoppers who want a festive appetizer without starting from scratch.

It may not replace a substantial charcuterie spread, but as a decorative addition to a holiday table, it offers something a little different from the usual cheese-and-cracker platter.
